The same limit of detection was obtained with both methods, and two cycles earlier detection with the LCC method was observed.

titre: Exposure to toxic environmental agents.
resume_court: : Reducing exposure to toxic environmental agents is a critical area of intervention for obstetricians, gynecologists, and other reproductive health care professionals.

titre: Molecular imaging of prostate cancer with PET.
resume_court: Molecular imaging is paving the way for precision and personalized medicine. In view of the significant biologic and clinical heterogeneity of prostate cancer, molecular imaging is expected to play an important role in the evaluation of this prevalent disease.

titre: Depression and the risk of cancer: a 15-year follow-up study of the GAZEL cohort.
resume_court: Depression has long been hypothesized to be associated with cancer incidence. In the present study, we examined the association between various measures of depression and cancer incidence at several sites. Overall, there was no compelling evidence for an association between depression and cancer incidence.

titre: NSC126188 induces apoptosis of prostate cancer PC-3 cells through inhibition of Akt membrane translocation, FoxO3a activation, and RhoB transcription.
resume_court: We previously reported that NSC126188 caused apoptosis of cancer cells by inducing expression of RhoB. Conversely, FoxO3a knockdown reduced NSC126188-induced RhoB expression and cell death. Taken together, NSC126188 induces apoptosis of PC-3 cells by interfering with membrane recruitment of Akt, resulting in Akt dephosphorylation and FoxO3a activation, which leads to transcription of RhoB.

titre: Relationship between multidrug resistance 1 polymorphisms and the risk of prostate cancer in Chinese populations.
resume_court: Prostate cancer is one of the most common malignancies in men. MDR1 gene polymorphism and its association with the risk of prostate cancer were investigated in 357 Chinese men. These findings suggested that the c.1465C>T polymorphism of MDR1 may be risk factors for prostate cancer in Chinese men.

titre: Evaluation of the PET component of simultaneous [(18)F]choline PET/MRI in prostate cancer: comparison with [(18)F]choline PET/CT.
resume_court: Median SUVmax and SUVmean of all lesions were significantly lower in PET/MRI than in PET/CT (5.2 vs 6.1, p<0.05 and 2.0 vs 2.6, p<0.001, respectively). PET image quality of PET/MRI was comparable to that of PET/CT. Both SUVmax and SUVmean were significantly lower in [(18)F]choline PET/MRI than in [(18)F]choline PET/CT.

titre: Percutaneous image-guided biopsy of prostate cancer metastases yields samples suitable for genomics and personalised oncology.
resume_court: Personalised oncology through mutational profiling of cancers requires the procurement of fresh frozen tumour samples for genomics applications. Our study aimed to determine the suitability of extracted nucleic acids for genomics applications using distant metastatic prostate cancer samples obtained via percutaneous or surgical biopsy.

titre: Prostate cancer stem cell-targeted efficacy of a new-generation taxoid, SBT-1214 and novel polyenolic zinc-binding curcuminoid, CMC2.24.

Importantly, this drug combination induced expression of p21 and p53, which were absent in CD133(high)/CD44(high) cells. We report here that the SBT-1214 alone, or in combination with CMC2.24, possesses significant activity against prostate CD133(high)/CD44(+/high) tumor-initiating cells.

titre: Early human prostate adenocarcinomas harbor androgen-independent cancer cells.
resume_court: Although blockade of androgen receptor (AR) signaling represents the main treatment for advanced prostate cancer (PrCa), many patients progress to a lethal phenotype of "Castration-Resistant" prostate cancer (CR-PrCa). We report here the propagation of Cancer Initiating Cells (CIC) directly from Stage I human PrCa tissue without selection or genetic manipulation.

titre: Mortality following hip fracture in men with prostate cancer.
resume_court: Hip fractures are associated with increased mortality and are a known adverse effect of androgen deprivation therapy (ADT) for prostate cancer (PCa). This risk was especially increased during the first month (5.64 (95%CI: 4.16-7.48)). Hip fractures are associated with higher all-cause mortality in PCa men on ADT than in PCa men not on ADT or PCa-free men, especially within the first three months.

titre: Reduced mitochondrial DNA content associates with poor prognosis of prostate cancer in African American men.
resume_court: Reduction or depletion of mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) has been associated with cancer progression. We provide the first evidence that tumors in AA men possess reduced level of mtDNA compared to CA men. Together, our data suggest that AA men possess lower mtDNA levels in normal and tumor tissues compared to CA men, which could contribute to higher risk and more aggressive prostate cancer in AA men.

titre: Impact of glutathione-S-transferases (GST) polymorphisms and hypermethylation of relevant genes on risk of prostate cancer biochemical recurrence: a meta-analysis.
resume_court: Accurate prediction of the biochemical recurrence (BCR) is critical for patients after intended curative therapy like radical prostatectomy (RP) or definitive radiotherapy for prostate cancer. To evaluate the relationship between glutathione-S-transferases polymorphisms and hypermethylation of these genes and the risk of prostate cancer BCR, we carried out a meta-analysis of the published studies.

titre: Sodium butyrate induces growth inhibition and apoptosis in human prostate cancer DU145 cells by up-regulation of the expression of annexin A1.

titre: Hedgehog signaling regulates telomerase reverse transcriptase in human cancer cells.

These results identify hTERT as a direct target of the HH signaling pathway, and reveal a previously unknown role of the HH/GLI axis in regulating the replication potential of cancer cells.

titre: Sorafenib sensitizes solid tumors to Apo2L/TRAIL and Apo2L/TRAIL receptor agonist antibodies by the Jak2-Stat3-Mcl1 axis.

titre: New pyrazolopyrimidine inhibitors of protein kinase d as potent anticancer agents for prostate cancer cells.

Analysis of several related kinases indicated that 1-NA-PP1 was highly selective for PKD as compared to IKK-16.

titre: Pituitary apoplexy induced by Gonadotropin-releasing hormone agonists for treating prostate cancer-report of first Asian case.

Headache, ophthalmoplegia, visual field deficit, nausea, and vomiting are the typical characteristics of pituitary apoplexy.

titre: Childhood height and birth weight in relation to future prostate cancer risk: a cohort study based on the copenhagen school health records register.

titre: Predicting risk of bladder cancer using clinical and demographic information from prostate, lung, colorectal, and ovarian cancer screening trial participants.

titre: Cancer risk estimates from radiation therapy for heterotopic ossification prophylaxis after total hip arthroplasty.

It is also the first non-denaturing chromatographic method reported for siRNA quantitation.

titre: Large oncosomes mediate intercellular transfer of functional microRNA.
resume_court: Prostate cancer cells release atypically large extracellular vesicles (EVs), termed large oncosomes, which may play a role in the tumor microenvironment by transporting bioactive molecules across tissue spaces and through the blood stream.

titre: Methylarsonous acid causes oxidative DNA damage in cells independent of the ability to biomethylate inorganic arsenic.
resume_court: Inorganic arsenic (iAs) and its toxic methylated metabolite, methylarsonous acid (MMA(III)), both have carcinogenic potential. Various metrics of oncogenic transformation were periodically assessed along with ODD during chronic MMA(III) exposure. Together, these results show that MMA(III) and iAs cause an acquired malignant phenotype in methylation-deficient cells, yet iAs does not induce ODD.

titre: Dietary carbohydrate intake, glycemic index, and glycemic load and endometrial cancer risk: a prospective cohort study.
resume_court: Endometrial cancer risk has been directly associated with glycemic load. Our aim was to investigate associations of carbohydrate intake, glycemic index, and glycemic load with endometrial cancer risk in the US Prostate, Lung, Colorectal and Ovarian Cancer Screening Trial. No associations with endometrial cancer risk were observed for glycemic index or dietary fiber.

titre: Diagnostic accuracy of 18F choline PET/CT using time-of-flight reconstruction algorithm in prostate cancer patients with biochemical recurrence.
resume_court: Image quality (IQ) of PET in voluminous body regions can be limited, which impairs the assessment of small metastatic lesions. The purpose of this study was to evaluate the impact of TOF on IQ, lesion detection rate, lesion volume (V) and SUVmax in F choline PET/CT of prostate cancer patients with biochemical recurrence compared to standard PET/CT reconstruction (standard).

titre: The PFP/RAG2 double-knockout mouse in metastasis research: small-cell lung cancer and prostate cancer.
resume_court: Patients with small-cell lung cancer (SCLC) and prostate cancer (PCa) as well as other solid tumors may have micro- or macro-metastatic spread at an early stage of the disease. SCLC and PCa xenograft transfer models in immunodeficient mice fail to model this metastatic spread in vivo. As a result NK cell activity directly influences treatment options and mortality.

titre: Functional relevance of D,L-sulforaphane-mediated induction of vimentin and plasminogen activator inhibitor-1 in human prostate cancer cells.
resume_court: D,L-Sulforaphane (SFN) is a promising chemopreventive agent with in vivo efficacy against prostate cancer in experimental rodents. Similar to vimentin, PAI-1 knockdown resulted in a modest augmentation of PC-3 cell migration inhibition by SFN. The present study indicates that vimentin and PAI-1 inductions confer modest protection against SFN-mediated inhibition of prostate cancer cell migration.

titre: Cancer mortality among psychiatric patients treated in a community-based system of care: a 25-year case register study.
resume_court: Cancer mortality data allow assessing, at the same time, the risk of developing the disease and the quality of care provided to patients after the oncologic diagnosis. Data were drawn from the South Verona Psychiatric Case Register (PCR). Chronic use of phenothiazines could be involved in the relative protection from stomach and prostate cancer found in psychiatric patients.

titre: Variability of assay methods for total and free PSA after WHO standardization.
resume_court: The variability of total PSA (tPSA) and free PSA (fPSA) results among commercial assays has been suggested to be decreased by calibration to World Health Organization (WHO) reference materials. At a critical concentration of 20 and 25 %, ADVIA Centaur XP, ARCHITECT i2000, and IMMULITE 2000 assays exceeded the 10 % relative difference limit.

titre: High expression of nucleobindin 2 mRNA: an independent prognostic factor for overall survival of patients with prostate cancer.
resume_court: Nucleobindin 2 (NUCB2) has been demonstrated to play critical roles in tumorigenesis and tumor development of breast cancer. However, the correlation between the expression of the NUCB2 mRNA and the overall survival of patients with PCa was not analyzed. In conclusion, we demonstrated that high NUCB2 mRNA expression correlated with poor overall survival in patients with PCa.

titre: Prostate-specific antigen screening trials and prostate cancer deaths: the androgen deprivation connection.
resume_court: Major clinical trials using prostate-specific antigen (PSA) as the screening test to detect localized early-stage prostate cancer and to attempt to change its natural history with early intervention have yielded conflicting interpretations. These divergent outcomes have not provided physicians with clarity on the best evidence-based treatment.

titre: Redox-mediated and ionizing-radiation-induced inflammatory mediators in prostate cancer development and treatment.
resume_court: Radiation therapy is widely used for treatment of prostate cancer. Multiple proinflammatory mediators can also influence redox status in irradiated cells and the surrounding microenvironment, thereby affecting prostate cancer progression and radiotherapy efficiency. Ionizing radiation (IR)-generated oxidative stress can regulate and be regulated by the production of proinflammatory mediators.

titre: Association of XPC gene polymorphisms with susceptibility to prostate cancer: evidence from 3,936 subjects.
resume_court: Polymorphisms of xeroderma pigmentosum complementation group C (XPC) are thought to have significant effects on prostate cancer (PCa) risk. We detected a significant association of PAT+/-polymorphism with PCa (p<0.05). In stratification analysis, we did not detect a significant association of PAT+/-polymorphism with risk of bone metastasis in PCa patients (p>0.05).

titre: CD24+/CD38- as new prognostic marker for non-small cell lung cancer.
resume_court: Lung cancer is the leading cause of death among cancers in the world. The combined CD24+/CD38-/low phenotype was detected in 50% of the cell lines that are also positive for CD133 and EpCAM. We report that CD24+/CD38-/low signature could potentially be used as a new biomarker for the early detection of NSCLC.

titre: Changing trends in symptomatology, diagnostics, stage and survival of prostate cancer in Northern Finland during a period of 20 years.
resume_court: Prostate cancer is the most common cancer among men in many countries. The 5-year prostate cancer-specific survival improved significantly over the 20 years. Further, prostate cancer-specific survival improved significantly over the period.

titre: Predicting survival of patients with node-positive prostate cancer following multimodal treatment.
resume_court: According to the TNM staging system, patients with prostate cancer (PCa) with lymph node invasion (LNI) are considered a single-risk group. Some patients with pN1 PCa have favorable CSM-free rates at 10 yr. We developed and internally validated the first nomograms that allow an accurate prediction of the CSM-free rate in these patients at an individual level.

titre: Simulation of realistic linac motion improves the accuracy of a Monte Carlo based VMAT plan QA system.
resume_court: To investigate the use of a software-based pre-treatment QA system for VMAT, which incorporates realistic linac motion during delivery. The ability to accurately calculate dose as a second check of the planning system, and determine realistic delivery characteristics, may allow for the reduction of machine-based pre-treatment plan QA for VMAT.

titre: Urinary outcomes are significantly affected by nerve sparing quality during radical prostatectomy.
resume_court: To assess the effect of nerve sparing (NS) quality on self-reported patient urinary outcomes after radical prostatectomy. Completely sparing at least 1 neurovascular bundle along with its supportive tissues has a dramatic effect on the recovery of urinary continence and quality of life in preoperatively potent men.

titre: When less is more: a simple predictive model for repeated prostate biopsy outcomes.
resume_court: To present a new predictive model for repeated prostate biopsy outcomes. Of the 221 patients, 29 (13%) were diagnosed with prostate cancer on the repeated biopsy. The simple graphical outcome makes the model even more attractive.

titre: Design, syntheses, and characterization of pharmacophore based chemokine receptor CCR5 antagonists as anti prostate cancer agents.
resume_court: Accumulating evidence has shown multiple roles that chemokine receptor CCR5 may play to promote the progression of several types of cancer. Therefore, blocking CCR5 function with an antagonist may provide a novel treatment of cancers such as prostate cancer. Results from this study provided a potential lead compound for future CCR5 antagonist development focusing on prostate cancer therapy.

titre: In vivo antiprostate tumor potential of Vernonia guineensis Benth. (Asteraceae) tuber extract (VGDE) and the cytotoxicity of its major compound pentaisovaleryl sucrose.
resume_court: Vernonia guineensis Benth. The aim of this study was to validate the claimed antiprostate cancer activity of Vernonia guineensis Benth. in vivo and to investigate the cytotoxicity of a pentaisovaleryl sucrose isolated from Vernonia guineensis on some cancer cell lines. A crude dichloromethane extract of Vernonia guineensis (VGDE) was used for this study.

titre: Impact of folate intake on prostate cancer recurrence following definitive therapy: data from CaPSURE™.
resume_court: A randomized, placebo controlled clinical trial of folic acid supplementation for the chemoprevention of colorectal adenoma revealed an increased incidence of prostate cancer in the treatment group. In patients treated with external beam radiation and brachytherapy we observed no evidence of an association between prostate cancer progression and increased folate intake.

titre: A common nonsense mutation of the BLM gene and prostate cancer risk and survival.
resume_court: Germline mutations of BRCA2 and NBS1 genes cause inherited recessive chromosomal instability syndromes and predispose to prostate cancer of poor prognosis. The 5-year survival for men with a BLM mutation was 83%, compared to 72% for mutation-negative cases. BLM Q548X is a common founder mutation in Poland.

titre: Second malignancies in long-term testicular cancer survivors.
resume_court: The objective of the present study is to analyze long-term testicular cancer (TC) survivors focusing on the correlation of therapeutic modalities used, the age of patients and second malignancy (SM) occurrence. Prostate cancer appeared in 10 patients (SIR 5.2), with a mean age 54.9 years, while the typical age of patients in Slovakia was 71.4 years. Other SM had no significantly higher SIR.

titre: The value of the 2005 International Society of Urological Pathology (ISUP) modified Gleason grading system as a predictor of biochemical recurrence after radical prostatectomy.
resume_court: To compare time and risk to biochemical recurrence (BR) after radical prostatectomy of two chronologically different groups of patients using the standard and the modified Gleason system (MGS). Time to BR using the Kaplan-Meier curves showed statistical significance using the MGS in cohort 2, but not the SGS in cohort 1.

titre: Do robotic prostatectomy positive surgical margins occur in the same location as extraprostatic extension?
resume_court: Positive surgical margins (PSMs) may reflect incomplete surgical resection, while extraprostatic extension (EPE) could suggest that complete tumor resection is more difficult. 51.8 % of the cases had EPE and PSM in discordant locations, 19.6 % had EPE and PSM in the same location, and 28.6 % had areas of EPE and PSM both in the same location as well as in different locations.

titre: Prostate cancer survivors as community health educators: implications for informed decision making and cancer communication.
resume_court: Recent evidence questioning the effectiveness of prostate-specific antigen testing leave community-based prostate cancer (CaP) outreach programs with a dilemma between promoting screening and highlighting screening risks. Training CaP survivors as health educators might be a viable strategy for community-based cancer communication efforts confronted by the CaP screening controversy.

titre: HOXB13 downregulates intracellular zinc and increases NF-?B signaling to promote prostate cancer metastasis.
resume_court: Characteristically, prostate cancer (PCa) cells exhibit marked decrease in intracellular zinc; however, the mechanism responsible is not clearly understood. Furthermore, exogenous HOXB13 caused intracellular zinc concentrations to fall in PCa cells, stimulated NF-?B-mediated signaling by reducing inhibitor of NF-?B alpha (I?Ba) and enhanced the nuclear translocation of RelA/p65.

titre: A case of colon cancer incidentally detected by 18F-choline PET/CT.
resume_court: A 65-year-old man had restaging of prostate cancer with an 18F-choline PET/CT, which revealed focal uptake in a thickened posterior wall of sigmoid colon. Biopsy demonstrated colon cancer. Incidental colorectal 18F-choline uptake should be further investigated with histological analysis.

titre: Locally advanced prostate cancer: optimal therapy in older patients.
resume_court: There is no standard treatment for locally advanced prostate cancer. Conservatively treated locally advanced prostate cancer is associated with poor survival outcome. In this article we discuss aspects of the management of locally advanced prostate cancer in the elderly with special focus on the recommendation of current clinical guidelines.

titre: Cabozantinib inhibits prostate cancer growth and prevents tumor-induced bone lesions.
resume_court: Using human prostate cancer xenograft studies in mice, we determined the impact of cabozantinib on tumor growth in soft tissue and bone. These data indicate that cabozantinib has direct antitumor activity, and that its ability to modulate osteoblast activity may contribute to its antitumor efficacy.

titre: Identifying cancer specific functionally relevant miRNAs from gene expression and miRNA-to-gene networks using regularized regression.
resume_court: Identifying microRNA signatures for the different types and subtypes of cancer can result in improved detection, characterization and understanding of cancer and move us towards more personalized treatment strategies. We present a method for the selection of biologically active microRNAs using gene expression data and microRNA-to-gene interaction network.

titre: Acid ceramidase promotes nuclear export of PTEN through sphingosine 1-phosphate mediated Akt signaling.
resume_court: We found that acid ceramidase promotes a reduction in nuclear PTEN that is dependent upon sphingosine 1-phosphate-mediated activation of Akt. These findings suggest that acid ceramidase, through sphingosine 1-phosphate, promotes nuclear export of PTEN as a means of promoting tumor formation, cell proliferation, and resistance to therapy.

titre: A three-marker FISH panel detects more genetic aberrations of AR, PTEN and TMPRSS2/ERG in castration-resistant or metastatic prostate cancers than in primary prostate tumors.
resume_court: TMPRSS2/ERG rearrangement, PTEN gene deletion, and androgen receptor (AR) gene amplification have been observed in various stages of human prostate cancer. Among samples with complete data available, the three-marker FISH panel detected chromosomal abnormalities in 53% of primary prostate cancers and 87% of metastatic (Met) or castration-resistant (CRPC) tumors.

titre: 20-years of population-based cancer registration in hepatitis B and liver cancer prevention in the Gambia, West Africa.
resume_court: The Gambia Hepatitis Intervention Study (GHIS) was designed as a randomised control trial of infant hepatitis B vaccination applied to public health policy, with the main goal of preventing primary liver cancer later in adult life in The Gambia. At the moment the data is not enough to detect an effect of hepatitis B vaccination on liver cancer incidence in The Gambia.

titre: Four microRNAs promote prostate cell proliferation with regulation of PTEN and its downstream signals in vitro.
resume_court: Phosphatase and tensin homologue (PTEN), as a tumor suppressor, plays vital roles in tumorigenesis and progression of prostate cancer. However, the mechanisms of PTEN regulation still need further investigation. These results suggested that the four miRNAs could promote prostate cancer cell proliferation by co-regulating the expression of PTEN, PI3K/Akt pathway and cyclin D1 in vitro.

titre: Advances in the formulations of non-injection administration of docetaxel.
resume_court: Docetaxel is one of the most important anti-tumor drugs and has shown powerful therapeutic activity against breast cancer, non-small cell lung cancer, prostate cancer and so on. In this review, the non-injection delivery formulations of docetaxel for oral route, transdermal delivery, lung and rectal administration were discussed for future study and clinical application.

titre: Sirolimus encapsulated liposomes for cancer therapy: physicochemical and mechanical characterization of sirolimus distribution within liposome bilayers.
resume_court: Sirolimus has recently been introduced as a therapeutic agent for breast and prostate cancer. In the current study, conventional and Stealth liposomes were used as carriers for the encapsulation of sirolimus. Similar results were obtained by differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) studies; sirolimus loaded liposomes were found to result in a distorted state of the bilayer.

titre: Pinoresinol inhibits proliferation and induces differentiation on human HL60 leukemia cells.
resume_court: Pinoresinol (PIN), one of the simplest lignans, is the precursor of other dietary lignans that are present in whole-grain cereals, legumes, fruits, and other vegetables. PIN caused an upregulation of the CDK inhibitor p21(WAF1/Cip1) both at mRNA and protein levels so suggesting that this could be a mechanism by which PIN reduced proliferation and induced differentiation on HL60 cells.

titre: Design of a phase I clinical trial to evaluate intratumoral delivery of ErbB-targeted chimeric antigen receptor T-cells in locally advanced or recurrent head and neck cancer.
resume_court: Despite several advances, 5-year survival in patients with head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) remains unchanged at only 50%. To exploit this, we have designed a first-in-man clinical trial in which T4(+) T-cells are administered to patients with locally advanced/recurrent HNSCC. Cells will be administered at a single sitting to multiple sites around the viable tumor circumference.

titre: Phase I dose-finding study of cabazitaxel administered weekly in patients with advanced solid tumours.
resume_court: Cabazitaxel is approved in patients with metastatic hormone-refractory prostate cancer previously treated with a docetaxel-containing regimen. Monitoring of DLTs was used to determine the MTD and the recommended weekly dose. The MTD of weekly cabazitaxel was 12 mg/m² and the recommended weekly dose was 10 mg/m².

titre: Efficacy and safety of abiraterone acetate in an elderly patient subgroup (aged 75 and older) with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer after docetaxel-based chemotherapy.
resume_court: Metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC) is a disease that primarily affects older men. To examine the efficacy and safety of AA plus P versus PL plus P in subgroups of elderly (aged = 75 yr) (n=331) and younger patients (<75 yr) (n=863). Patients were randomised 2:1 to AA (1000 mg) plus low-dose P (5mg twice daily) (n=797) or PL plus P (n=398).

titre: Diagnostic and predictive value of urine PCA3 gene expression for the clinical management of patients with altered prostatic specific antigen.
resume_court: Analyze the impact of the introduction of the study of PCA3 gene in post-prostatic massage urine in the clinical management of patients with PSA altered, evaluating its diagnostic ability and predictive value of tumor aggressiveness. Biopsy was only indicated in cases with s-positive PCA3. The s-PCA3 was positive in 43.7% of samples.

titre: Efficacy of oxaliplatin plus pemetrexed in chemotherapy pretreated metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer.
resume_court: Although new androgen-targeted therapies offer prolonged survival in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (CRPC), most men still face progressive disease and require additional therapy. Six of 15 evaluable patients (40%) experienced a pain response. Combination oxaliplatin and pemetrexed (PemOx) is an effective and tolerable second- or third-line treatment for men with CRPC.

titre: Image-guided intensity-modulated radiotherapy for prostate cancer: Dose constraints for the anterior rectal wall to minimize rectal toxicity.
resume_court: Rectal adverse events (AEs) are a major concern with definitive radiotherapy (RT) treatment for prostate cancer. This study evaluated the absolute volume of anterior rectal wall receiving a high dose to identify potential ideal dose constraints that can minimize rectal AEs. At 5 years, the cumulative incidence of late rectal AEs was 37%, with only 5% being grade =2.

titre: Androgen induces a switch from cytoplasmic retention to nuclear import of the androgen receptor.
resume_court: The androgen receptor (AR) has critical functions as a transcription factor in both normal and cancer cells, but the specific mechanisms that regulate its nuclear localization are not well defined. The bipartite NLS is recognized by importin 7, a nuclear import receptor for several proteins. Importin 7 binding to AR, however, inhibits import by shielding the bipartite NLS.

titre: Sodium meta-arsenite induces reactive oxygen species-dependent apoptosis, necrosis, and autophagy in both androgen-sensitive and androgen-insensitive prostate cancer cells.
resume_court: Sodium meta-arsenite (NaAsO2), a novel compound synthesized by Komipham International Co. Therefore, these results suggest that sodium meta-arsenite induces apoptotic, necrotic, and autophagic cell death through intracellular ROS accumulation in both androgen-sensitive and androgen-insensitive prostate cancer cells and may be used as a new anticancer drug for the treatment of prostate cancer.

titre: Zoledronic acid in the treatment of metastatic breast cancer.
resume_court: Bone is the most common location of metastatic disease. Approximately 80% of all bone metastases are observed in patients with breast or prostate tumours and are responsible for more than 300 000 deaths every year. Zoledronic acid is a bisphosphonate that has been shown to delay or prevent the development of skeletal-related events in patients with bone metastases.

titre: Tumor necrosis factor receptor associated factor-4: an adapter protein overexpressed in metastatic prostate cancer is regulated by microRNA-29a.
resume_court: The tumor necrosis factor receptor (TNFR)-associated factor 4 (TRAF4) is a member of TRAF family proteins that act as major signal transducers of the TNF receptor and the interleukin-1 receptor/Toll-like receptor (IL-1R/TLR) superfamily. Considered together, our results suggest that the tumor suppressor microRNA, miR-29a, is one of the regulators of TRAF4 expression in metastatic prostate cancer.

titre: MLS-2384, a new 6-bromoindirubin derivative with dual JAK/Src kinase inhibitory activity, suppresses growth of diverse cancer cells.
resume_court: Janus kinase (JAK) and Src kinase are the two major tyrosine kinase families upstream of signal transducer and activator of transcription (STAT). Our findings support further development of MLS-2384 as a potential small-molecule therapeutic agent that targets JAK, Src, and STAT3 signaling in multiple human cancer cells.

titre: Exercise therapy for sexual dysfunction after prostate cancer.
resume_court: Sexual dysfunction is one of the most common, distressing and persistent adverse effects of prostate cancer treatment, and has a profound effect on quality of life for the patient and his partner. Emerging evidence indicates that exercise also has a positive effect on sexual desire and sexual activity in men with prostate cancer.

titre: A novel resveratrol analogue, HS-1793, inhibits hypoxia-induced HIF-1a and VEGF expression, and migration in human prostate cancer cells.
resume_court: In many studies, resveratrol has been shown to have a chemopreventive effect in various types of cancer cells. This study investigated the effects of a novel analogue of resveratrol, HS-1793, on the expression of HIF-1a and vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) in PC-3 human prostate cancer cells. Mechanistically, HS-1793 inhibited HIF-1a and VEGF expression through multiple mechanisms.

titre: Aberrant expression of the PRAC gene in prostate cancer.
resume_court: Identification of aberrant expression patterns of genes in prostate cancer (PCa) is a key step towards the development of effective therapies. Thus, our findings suggest that the pathogenesis of PCa may be due to the expression levels of PRAC protein, and this protein can serve as a potential biomarker for the management of PCa.

titre: The effect of the frequency and duration of PSA measurement on PSA doubling time calculations in men with biochemically recurrent prostate cancer.
resume_court: PSA doubling time (PSADT) is an attractive intermediate end point for assessing novel therapies in biochemically recurrent prostate cancer (BRPC). Approximately 30% of JHH men experienced >200% increases in PSADT. Placebo-controlled RCTs including clinical end points are recommended to screen novel agents in men with BRPC to mitigate bias because of natural PSADT variability.

titre: Emerging association between androgen deprivation therapy and male meningioma: significant expression of luteinizing hormone-releasing hormone receptor in male meningioma.
resume_court: There is emerging data suggesting a potential risk for meningioma growth stimulation in patients on luteinizing hormone-releasing hormone (LHRH) analogs for prostate cancer. PR was positive in 20 of 24 (83%) MM and 23 of 24 (96%) FM samples. Caution should be taken when considering LHRH agonist administration for patients with PCa and concurrent meningioma or previous history of meningioma.

titre: Metformin does not affect risk of biochemical recurrence following radical prostatectomy: results from the SEARCH database.
resume_court: While epidemiologic studies suggest that metformin use among diabetics may decrease prostate cancer (PC) incidence, the effect of metformin use on PC outcome is unclear. Unadjusted analysis suggested that high metformin dose vs non-use was associated with increased risk of CRPC (HR 5.1; 95% CI 1.6-16.5), metastases (HR 4.8; 95% CI 1.2-18.5) and PC-specific mortality (HR 5.0; 95% CI 1.1-22.5).

titre: Beyond abiraterone: new hormonal therapies for metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer.
resume_court: Prostate cancer is a heterogeneous disease where the previous concept of "hormone resistance" has been changed by a new generation of hormonal therapies that have proven efficacy in the castration-resistant setting. In this review the development of new hormonal therapies following the arrival of abiraterone for the treatment of prostate cancer will be summarized.

titre: Investigating a pathogenic role for TXNDC5 in tumors.
resume_court: The expression of TXNDC5, which is induced by hypoxia, stimulates cell proliferation and angiogenesis. The increased cell proliferation, angiogenesis and hypoxia are main features of tumor tissues. The present study aimed to characterize the expression of TXNDC5 in various tumor types and to investigate the role of TXNDC5 in the growth, proliferation and migration of tumor cells.

titre: Robot assisted laparoscopic prostatectomy in 2013.
resume_court: Robot assisted laparoscopic prostatectomy has surpassed open radical prostatectomy as the most common surgical approach for radical prostatectomy in the United States. In this article we briefly describe the evolution of this minimally invasive technique. Finally we present a critical appraisal of the published oncological, continence and potency outcomes.

titre: Randomized trial of hypofractionated external-beam radiotherapy for prostate cancer.
resume_court: To determine if escalated radiation dose using hypofractionation significantly reduces biochemical and/or clinical disease failure (BCDF) in men treated primarily for prostate cancer. The primary end point was the cumulative incidence of BCDF. The 5-year rates of BCDF were 21.4% (95% CI, 14.8% to 28.7%) for CIMRT and 23.3% (95% CI, 16.4% to 31.0%) for HIMRT (P = .745).

titre: Prostate-specific antigen changes as surrogate for overall survival in men with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer treated with second-line chemotherapy.
resume_court: Prostate-specific antigen (PSA) kinetics, and more specifically a = 30% decline in PSA within 3 months after initiation of first-line chemotherapy with docetaxel, are associated with improvement in overall survival (OS) in men with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC). The PTE for a = 30% decline in PSA was 0.34 (95% CI, 0.11 to 0.56), indicating a lack of surrogacy for OS.

titre: Generation of prostate tumor-initiating cells is associated with elevation of reactive oxygen species and IL-6/STAT3 signaling.
resume_court: How prostate cancer is initiated remains a topic of debate. Importantly, a positive feedback loop was found between ROS and IL-6 during tumor sphere formation. The intrinsic association of ROS and IL-6/STAT3 signaling in human prostate carcinogenesis shed new light on this relationship and define therapeutic targets in this setting.

titre: TALEN-engineered AR gene rearrangements reveal endocrine uncoupling of androgen receptor in prostate cancer.
resume_court: Androgen receptor (AR) target genes direct development and survival of the prostate epithelial lineage, including prostate cancer (PCa). These findings demonstrate that AR gene rearrangements are a unique resistance mechanism by which AR transcriptional activity can be uncoupled from endocrine regulation in CRPC.

titre: miRNA and mRNA cancer signatures determined by analysis of expression levels in large cohorts of patients.
resume_court: Toward identifying a cancer-specific gene signature we applied surprisal analysis to the RNAs expression behavior for a large cohort of breast, lung, ovarian, and prostate carcinoma patients. The miRNA and mRNA networks are common to the noncancer and cancer patients, but the disease modulates the strength of the connectivities.

titre: Robotics in uro-oncologic surgery.
resume_court: In urology, the main use for the robotic technique has been in radical prostatectomy for prostate cancer. The objective of this article is to offer an overview of all robotic procedures recently developed in the field of urology. Comparative data and an adequate follow-up are needed to demonstrate equivalent oncologic outcomes in comparison with traditional open or laparoscopic procedures.

titre: Robotic prostatectomy: an update on functional and oncologic outcomes.
resume_court: Since the first procedure performed in 2000, robotic-assisted radical prostatectomy (RARP) has been rapidly gaining increasing acceptance from both urologists and patients. We also evaluate the potential advantages of RARP in comparison with open and laparoscopic procedures.

titre: Genito-urological cancers in elderly patients.
resume_court: Age is now widely accepted as the greatest single risk factor for developing cancer, and cancer is considered primarily as a disease of the elderly. This review takes a look to the tumor biology and to the morbidity of cancer treatment in elderly patients affected by genito-urological cancer like prostate, bladder and renal cancer.

titre: The reasons behind variation in Gleason grading of prostatic biopsies: areas of agreement and misconception among 266 European pathologists.
resume_court: The Gleason scoring system underwent revision at the International Society of Urological Pathology (ISUP) conference in 2005. Any amount of secondary pattern of higher grade in needle biopsies was included in the Gleason score by 58%. Tertiary GP of higher grade on needle biopsies was included in the Gleason score by only 58%.

titre: Mechanism of androgen receptor corepression by CKßBP2/CRIF1, a multifunctional transcription factor coregulator expressed in prostate cancer.
resume_court: The transcription factor coregulator Casein kinase IIß-binding protein 2 or CR6-interacting factor 1 (CKßBP2/CRIF1) binds the androgen receptor (AR) in prostate cancer cells and in response to dihydrotestosterone localizes with AR on the prostate-specific antigen gene enhancer, but does not bind DNA suggesting CKßBP2/CRIF1 localization in chromatin is determined by AR.

titre: Characteristics of cases with unknown stage prostate cancer in a population-based cancer registry.
resume_court: The New South Wales Central Cancer Registry (NSW CCR) is the only population-based cancer registry in Australia that has routinely collected summary stage at diagnosis since its inception in 1972. However, a large proportion of prostate cancer cases have "unknown" stage recorded by the registry. Of 39852 prostate cancer cases, 41.8% had "unknown" stage recorded by the NSW CCR.

titre: Reversal of chemosensitivity and induction of cell malignancy of a non-malignant prostate cancer cell line upon extracellular vesicle exposure.
resume_court: Extracellular vesicle (EV) trafficking is a fundamental cellular process that occurs in cells and is required for different aspects of pathophysiology. Our study provides a rational basis to further investigate putative proteins, such as 14-3-3 and prohibitin and genetic factors that may be responsible for phenotypic changes that are associated with prostate cancer progression.

titre: Impact of an online survivorship primer on clinician knowledge and intended practice changes.
resume_court: The number of adult cancer survivors in the USA is expected to double by the year 2050. The results of this educational intervention demonstrated the effectiveness of internet-based CME/CE for cancer survivorship. Nearly 100% of participants agreed that the course contributed to survivorship care and was organized effectively.

titre: A comparative study of glycoproteomes in androgen-sensitive and -independent prostate cancer cell lines.
resume_court: Prostate cancer is one of the most common malignancies in men and is predicted to be the second leading cause of cancer-related deaths. After 6-18 months, hormone ablation treatment results in androgen-independent growth of cancer cells, metastasis and progression. The mechanism of androgen-independent growth of prostatic carcinoma cells is still unknown.

titre: First imaging results of an intraindividual comparison of (11)C-acetate and (18)F-fluorocholine PET/CT in patients with prostate cancer at early biochemical first or second relapse after prostatectomy or radiotherapy.
resume_court: (18)F-Fluorocholine (FCH) and (11)C-acetate (ACE) PET are widely used for detection of recurrent prostate cancer (PC). Lymph-node results were concordant in 19 patients and different in 4 patients. Overall, ACE and FCH PET/CT showed excellent concordance, on both a per-lesion and a per-patient basis, suggesting that both tracers perform equally for recurrent prostate cancer staging.

titre: Opioid requirement, opioid receptor expression, and clinical outcomes in patients with advanced prostate cancer.
resume_court: Preclinical studies show that opioids stimulate angiogenesis and tumor progression through the mu opioid receptor (MOR). Laser scanning confocal microscopy was used to analyze MOR immunoreactivity in prostate cancer biopsies. Higher MOR expression and greater opioid requirement are associated with shorter progression-free survival and overall survival in patients with metastatic prostate cancer.

titre: Concurrent chemoradiotherapy with low-dose docetaxel inhibits the growth of DU-145 prostate cancer xenografts.
resume_court: Concurrent chemoradiotherapy (CCRT) has been widely used during the past decades in clinical trials and has now become a common treatment option in many clinical settings. ×5, ×3 weeks), (4) CCRT (the combination of docetaxel and radiation). Based on these preclinical findings, we suggest that CCRT for the treatment of prostate cancer deserves further development.

titre: Ice application for reducing pain associated with goserelin acetate injection

titre: Messenger RNA vaccine based on recombinant MS2 virus-like particles against prostate cancer.

titre: Exploring glyoxalase 1 expression in prostate cancer tissues: targeting the enzyme by ethyl pyruvate defangs some malignancy-associated properties.

titre: Desquamation is a novel phenomenon for collective prostate epithelial cell deletion after castration.

titre: 125Iodine monotherapy for Japanese men with low- and intermediate-risk prostate cancer: outcomes after 5 years of follow-up.

Monotherapy with (125)I showed excellent outcomes with limited morbidity for Japanese men with low- and intermediate-risk prostate cancer after 5 years of follow-up.

titre: What lies within: novel strategies in immunotherapy for non-small cell lung cancer.
resume_court: Immunotherapy has become an increasingly important therapeutic strategy for those with cancer, with phase III studies demonstrating survival advantages in melanoma and castration-resistant prostate cancer. titre: A double-blind, randomized phase II study to evaluate the safety and efficacy of acetyl-L-carnitine in the prevention of sagopilone-induced peripheral neuropathy.

titre: Can selenium be a modifier of cancer risk in CHEK2 mutation carriers?

titre: Exosome encased spherical nucleic acid gold nanoparticle conjugates as potent microRNA regulation agents.

titre: Inguinal hernia developed after radical retropubic surgery for prostate cancer.

titre: Longitudinal prostate-specific antigen reference ranges: Choosing the underlying model of age-related changes.

titre: Mortality trends and years of potential life lost from prostate cancer in the 32 states and 7 sociecononomic regions of Mexico, 2000-2010

titre: Elevated fatty acid synthase expression in prostate needle biopsy cores predicts upgraded Gleason score in radical prostatectomy specimens.

titre: Molecular pathology and prostate cancer therapeutics: from biology to bedside.

titre: Orbital neoplasms in adults: clinical, radiologic, and pathologic review.

titre: Androgen regulation of the TMPRSS2 gene and the effect of a SNP in an androgen response element.

titre: Combination of intra-operative freehand SPECT imaging with MR images for guidance and navigation.

titre: Identifying candidate disease genes using a trace norm constrained bipartite raking model.

titre: Automatic prostate segmentation in cone-beam computed tomography images using rigid registration.

titre: Using CamiTK for rapid prototyping of interactive computer assisted medical intervention applications.

titre: Cancer talk on twitter: community structure and information sources in breast and prostate cancer social networks.

titre: Progression and predictors of physical activity levels after radical prostatectomy.

titre: Can we improve the definition of high-risk, hormone naïve, non-metastatic prostate cancer?

titre: A multicentre year-long randomised controlled trial of exercise training targeting physical functioning in men with prostate cancer previously treated with androgen suppression and radiation from TROG 03.04 RADAR.

titre: Lysophosphatidic acid induces reactive oxygen species generation by activating protein kinase C in PC-3 human prostate cancer cells.

titre: Evaluation of (-2)proPSA in combination with total PSA and free PSA for the early detection of prostate cancer

titre: Thermally targeted p21 peptide enhances bortezomib cytotoxicity in androgen-independent prostate cancer cell lines.

titre: The symptom burden of cancer: Evidence for a core set of cancer-related and treatment-related symptoms from the Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group Symptom Outcomes and Practice Patterns study.

titre: The prostate, lung, colorectal, and ovarian cancer screening trial and its associated research resource.
