titre: The significance of autoantibodies to DFS70/LEDGFp75 in health and disease: integrating basic science with clinical understanding.
resume_court: Antinuclear autoantibodies (ANAs) displaying the nuclear dense fine speckled immunofluorescence (DFS-IIF) pattern in HEp-2 substrates are commonly observed in clinical laboratory referrals. In this comprehensive review, we integrate our current knowledge of the biology of DFS70/LEDGFp75 with the clinical understanding of its autoantibodies in the contexts of health and disease.

titre: Combination of Pim kinase inhibitors and Bcl-2 antagonists in chronic lymphocytic leukemia cells.
resume_court: The Pim proteins are Ser/Thr kinases over-expressed in several hematological malignancies such as chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL) and some solid cancers like prostate cancer. This study evaluated the in vitro cytotoxic effect of three Pim kinase inhibitors (AZD1208, SGI-1776 and SMI-4a) combined with Bcl-2 antagonists (ABT-737 or ABT-199) in malignant CLL lymphocytes.

titre: A subset of prostatic basal cell carcinomas harbor the MYB rearrangement of adenoid cystic carcinoma.
resume_court: Adenoid cystic carcinoma (ACC) is a basaloid tumor consisting of myoepithelial and ductal cells typically arranged in a cribriform pattern. The MYB rearrangement was detected in 2 (29%) of 7 ACC-like carcinomas but in none (0%) of the 5 PBCCs with a prominent solid pattern. True ACCs can arise in the prostate as is evidenced by the presence of the characteristic MYB rearrangement.

titre: Recruitment and Participation of African American Men in Church-Based Health Promotion Workshops.
resume_court: Health promotion interventions in African American communities are frequently delivered in church settings. The current analysis discusses the men's participation rates in the M-PACT intervention, which consisted of a series of 4 bimonthly men's health workshops in 18 African American churches.

titre: Novel Anti-TM4SF1 Antibody-Drug Conjugates with Activity against Tumor Cells and Tumor Vasculature.
resume_court: Antibody-drug conjugates (ADC) represent a promising therapeutic modality for managing cancer. We hypothesized that an ADC against TM4SF1 would inhibit cancer growth directly by killing cancer cells and indirectly by attacking the tumor vasculature. As v1.10 did not react with mouse TM4SF1, it could not target the mouse tumor vasculature.

titre: Identification and Functional Validation of Reciprocal microRNA-mRNA Pairings in African American Prostate Cancer Disparities.
resume_court: African Americans (AA) exhibit higher rates of prostate cancer incidence and mortality compared with European American (EA) men. Novel miRNA-mRNA pairings were validated by qRT-PCR, Western blot, and/or IHC analyses in prostate cancer specimens. Our data suggest that AA-specific/-enriched miRNA-mRNA pairings may play a critical role in the activation of oncogenic pathways in AA prostate cancer.

titre: Radium-223 dichloride: illustrating the benefits of a multidisciplinary approach for patients with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer.
resume_court: Improving options for patients with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC) provide latitude in designing treatment plans that meet patients' medical needs and personal goals. In our clinic, radium-223 is used primarily to extend patient survival. Patient selection, patient management, and treatment sequencing are discussed here in the context of a multidisciplinary environment.

titre: Expression of some selected cytokeratins and Ki67 protein in prostatic tumor: can these be used as tumor markers.
resume_court: Diagnosis of prostatic diseases with Immunohistochemistry still faces challenges because of the peculiar histology of the prostate and difference(s) in reactivity of Monoclonal antibodies (MoAb) to benign and malignant changes. Ki67 was only reactive in 2(13.3) of BPH samples and 15(100%) of CaP. Only Ck 8 was expressed in both BPH and CaP.

titre: Cellular Adhesion Promotes Prostate Cancer Cells Escape from Dormancy.
resume_court: Dissemination of prostate cancer (PCa) cells to the bone marrow is an early event in the disease process. Here, we characterized in vitro PCa dormancy-reactivation by inducing cells from three patient-derived xenograft (PDX) lines to proliferate through tumor cell contact with each other and with bone marrow stroma.

titre: Age-Specific Cutoff Value for the Application of Percent Free Prostate-Specific Antigen (PSA) in Chinese Men with Serum PSA Levels of 4.0-10.0 ng/ml.
resume_court: The influence of age on the performance of percent free prostate-specific antigen (%fPSA) in diagnosing prostate cancer (PCa) in East Asians is controversial. The effectiveness of %fPSA is correlated with age in the Chinese population. Age-specific cutoff values would help avoid unnecessary biopsies in the Chinese population.

titre: Chromatin to Clinic: The Molecular Rationale for PARP1 Inhibitor Function.
resume_court: The molecular basis for PARP1 inhibitor function is complex, and appears to depend on the dual roles of PARP1 in DNA damage repair and transcriptional regulation. Here, the mechanisms by which PARP-1 inhibitors elicit clinical response are discussed, and strategies for translating the preclinical elucidation of PARP-1 function into advances in disease management are reviewed.

titre: Downregulation of c-SRC kinase CSK promotes castration resistant prostate cancer and pinpoints a novel disease subclass.
resume_court: SRC kinase is activated in castration resistant prostate cancer (CRPC), phosphorylates the androgen receptor (AR), and causes its ligand-independent activation as a transcription factor. These results identify CSK downregulation as a principal driver of SRC activation and castration resistance and validate SRC as a drug target in a molecularly defined subclass of CRPCs.

titre: Palliative pelvic radiotherapy for symptomatic incurable prostate cancer – A prospective multicenter study.
resume_court: Radiotherapy is used to palliate pelvic symptoms of castration resistant prostate cancer (CRPC). 47 patients with CRPC and a symptomatic pelvic mass prescribed PPRT with 30-39 Gy were prospectively included. In the majority of patients with CRPC and a symptomatic pelvic tumor, PPRT with 30-39 Gy contributes to relief of hematuria, pain and other pelvic symptoms, with acceptable toxicity.

titre: Re-distribution of brachytherapy dose using a differential dose prescription adapted to risk of local failure in low-risk prostate cancer patients.
resume_court: An intermediate-risk target volume (CTV(Prostate)) and a high-risk target volume (CTV(HR)=GTV+5 mm margin) were defined. Our risk adaptive target- and dose prescription concept of prescribing a lower dose to the whole gland and an escalated dose to the GTV using LDR-BT seed planning was technically feasible and resulted in a significant dose-reduction to urethra and bladder neck.

titre: Reducing Skeletal-Related Events in Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer.
resume_court: Skeletal-related events contribute substantially to morbidity, mortality and cost in men with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC). There are five agents available for treatment in mCRPC that reduce skeletal-related events. Finally, we review the available data regarding the cost of denosumab compared with that of zoledronic acid.

titre: Screening for Cervical, Prostate, and Breast Cancer: Interpreting the Evidence.
resume_court: Cancer screening is an important component of prevention and early detection in public health and clinical medicine. The evidence for cancer screening, however, is often contentious. If implemented, these strategies will improve the production and interpretation of the methodologically challenging and always-growing evidence for and against cancer screening.

titre: Prostate Cancer Unit Initiative in Europe: A position paper by the European School of Oncology.
resume_court: The Prostate Cancer Programme of the European School of Oncology developed the concept of specialised interdisciplinary and multiprofessional prostate cancer care to be formalized in Prostate Cancer Units (PCU). This position paper describes the relevant, feasible and applicable core criteria for defining PCUs in most European countries delivered by PCU Initiative in Europe Task Force.

titre: Feasibility study of a randomized controlled trial comparing docetaxel chemotherapy and androgen deprivation therapy with sequential prostatic biopsies from patients with advanced non-castration-resistant prostate cancer.
resume_court: Sequential tissue biopsies taken during clinical trials of novel systemic anticancer therapies for advanced prostate cancer (PCa) may aid pharmacodynamic evaluation and biomarker discovery. Transrectal ultrasound-guided prostatic biopsies were taken at randomization and ~22 weeks after treatment initiation. No adverse effects of pre- and post-treatment prostatic biopsies were observed.

titre: Cadherin-11 regulates the metastasis of Ewing sarcoma cells to bone.
resume_court: Ewing sarcoma (ES) is a small round-cell tumor of the bones and soft tissues. Here we investigated the effects of Cad-11 on bone metastases of ES. These findings may explain that Cad-11 in ES cells may be essential for cell adhesion and motility, and is a promising molecular target for patients with ES.

titre: A novel rabbit anti-hepatocyte growth factor monoclonal neutralizing antibody inhibits tumor growth in prostate cancer cells and mouse xenografts.
resume_court: The hepatocyte growth factor and its receptor c-Met are correlated with castration-resistance in prostate cancer. We selected one RabMAb with mouse cross-reactivity and demonstrated that it blocked HGF-stimulated downstream activation in PC-3 and DU145 cells. Anti-HGF RabMAb inhibited not only the growth of PC-3 cells but also HGF-dependent proliferation in HUVECs.

titre: Meralgia paraesthetica: Ultrasound-guided injection at multiple levels with 12-month follow-up.
resume_court: To evaluate the efficacy of ultrasound (US)-guided injections around the lateral femoral cutaneous nerve (LFCN) at different levels in meralgia paraesthetica (MP) patients. The outcome of US-guided injection along the LFCN can be further improved by injections at different levels (p?<?0.05), which was confirmed at 12-month long-term follow-up.

titre: The Importance of Prostate-specific Antigen (PSA) Nadir and Early Identification of PSA Relapse after 10 Years of Prostate Iodine 125 Seed Brachytherapy in Edinburgh.
resume_court: To analyse our 5 and 10 year prostate brachytherapy outcome data and to assess the impact of PSA nadir on relapse free survival and whether an alternative definition of PSA relapse could detect men destined to fail by the Phoenix definition at an earlier time point. The Phoenix definition of nadir plus 2.0 ng/ml does not allow the early identification of men destined to relapse.

titre: Image-based monitoring of targeted biopsy-proven prostate cancer on active surveillance: 11-year experience.
resume_court: To report our 11-year experience of Active Surveillance (AS) program focusing on modern transrectal ultrasound (TRUS)-based monitoring of targeted biopsy-proven cancer lesion. Doppler grade of blood flow signal within the lesion was classified from grade 0 to 3. The increase in diameter and upgrade of Doppler grade of the lesion were significant risk factors for biopsy-proven progression on AS.

titre: Hypocalcaemia in patients with metastatic bone disease treated with denosumab.
resume_court: This analysis was performed to further characterise treatment-emergent hypocalcaemia in patients with bone metastases receiving denosumab. Hypocalcaemia was more frequent with denosumab versus zoledronic acid, consistent with denosumab's greater antiresorptive effect. Adequate calcium and vitamin D intake appears to substantially reduce the risk of hypocalcaemia.

titre: Exploitation of the Androgen Receptor to Overcome Taxane Resistance in Advanced Prostate Cancer.
resume_court: Shifting the current paradigm is a growing evidence to indicate that Docetaxel can effectively target the AR signaling axis by blocking its nuclear translocation and transcriptional activity in androgen-sensitive and castration-resistant prostate cancer cells, implicating a new mechanism of cross-resistance between microtubule-targeting chemotherapy and antiandrogen therapies.

titre: Active nuclear IKK correlates with metastatic risk in cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma.
resume_court: About 5% of all cutaneous squamous cell carcinomas (cSCCs) metastasize, which is the principal cause of death by this type of cancer. Our results indicate that nuclear active IKK is a robust biomarker to predict cSCC outcome, and suggest the possibility of targeting IKK activity as a future therapy for treating metastatic cSCC.

titre: TREATMENT OF URINARY INCONTINENCE AFTER RADICAL PROSTATECTOMY USING TRAINING OF PELVIC MUSCLES UNDER THE CONTROL OF BIOFEEDBACK
resume_court: Urinary incontinence (UI) is one of the most frequent complications of radical prostatectomy (RPE) performed for prostate cancer. This method was applied in 87 patients who underwent radical prostatectomy. In patients with stable skill of isolated pelvic muscle contractions this parameter was 4 months, and in the absence of sustainable skill of isolated contractions - 9.4 months (p=0.001).

titre: EVALUATION OF DIAGNOSTIC SIGNIFICANCE OF PELVIC MRI IN PROSTATE CANCER PATIENTS
resume_court: Accurate staging of prostate cancer is a prerequisite to forecast disease progression and-to guide surgery planning. In current clinical practice, contrast-enhanced MRI is one of the imaging tools for improving the evaluation of prostate cancer patients. To assess the diagnostic value of MRI a retrospective study in a real clinical practice setting was conducted.

titre: VALUE OF THE -2PROPSA INDEX AND THE PROSTATE HEALTH INDEX IN PATIENTS WITH PROSTATE CANCER: REVIEW OF LITERATURE AND DATA OF RUSSIAN PROSPECTIVE STUDY
resume_court: The article presents the analysis of the fundamental studies on the -2proPSA and prostate health index (PHI) and the determination of their field of use in patients with prostate cancer (PCa).

titre: Relaxation along fictitious field, diffusion-weighted imaging, and T2 mapping of prostate cancer: Prediction of cancer aggressiveness.
resume_court: To evaluate the performance of relaxation along a fictitious field (RAFF) relaxation time (TRAFF ), diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI)-derived parameters, and T2 relaxation time values for prostate cancer (PCa) detection and characterization. TRAFF values had higher AUC values for Gleason score classification compared with DWI-derived parameters and T2 .

titre: A novel role for peptidylarginine deiminases in microvesicle release reveals therapeutic potential of PAD inhibition in sensitizing prostate cancer cells to chemotherapy.
resume_court: Our results reveal that during the stimulation of prostate cancer cells (PC3) to microvesiculate, PAD2 and PAD4 expression levels and the deimination of cytoskeletal actin are increased. Pharmacological inhibition of PAD enzyme activity using Cl-am significantly reduced MV release and abrogated the deimination of cytoskeletal actin.

titre: Screening for Occult Cancer in Unprovoked Venous Thromboembolism.
resume_court: Venous thromboembolism may be the earliest sign of cancer. We sought to assess the efficacy of a screening strategy for occult cancer that included comprehensive computed tomography (CT) of the abdomen and pelvis in patients who had a first unprovoked venous thromboembolism. The prevalence of occult cancer was low among patients with a first unprovoked venous thromboembolism.

titre: Observational and genetic plasma YKL-40 and cancer in 96,099 individuals from the general population.
resume_court: Plasma YKL-40 is high in patients with cancer and in individuals who later develop cancer. Plasma levels of YKL-40 were measured in 21,643 and CHI3L1 rs4950928 was genotyped in 94,568 individuals. This study shows that high plasma YKL-40 levels were associated with high risk of gastrointestinal and likely of lung cancer, but genetic high levels were not.

titre: Optimization of multi-stage dynamic treatment regimes utilizing accumulated data.
resume_court: In medical therapies involving multiple stages, a physician's choice of a subject's treatment at each stage depends on the subject's history of previous treatments and outcomes. We consider dynamic treatment regimes in settings where each subject's final outcome can be defined as the sum of longitudinally observed values, each corresponding to a stage of the regime.

titre: Gamma index comparison of three VMAT QA systems and evaluation of their sensitivity to delivery errors.
resume_court: To compare detectors for dosimetric verification before VMAT treatments and evaluate their sensitivity to errors. It was found that for the plans delivered with errors, the sensitivity was quite similar for all devices. All three devices have the potential to detect errors with more or less the same threshold.

titre: Adherence to the lymphadenectomy recommendations of the 2009 clinical guidelines in the 2010 National Prostate Cancer Registry.
resume_court: To assess the adherence to the recommendations of the 2009 clinical guidelines in the implementation of lymphadenectomy during radical prostatectomy and analysis of the variables that influence this decision in the 2010 National Prostate Cancer Registry. The raw agreement with the EAU-09 clinical guidelines was .672 (.48-.96 in the various centers), and the kappa index was .289.

titre: Exploration on natural product anibamine side chain modification toward development of novel CCR5 antagonists and potential anti-prostate cancer agents.
resume_court: Prostate cancer is one of the leading causes of death among males in the world. Anibamine, a natural product containing a pyridine ring and two aliphatic side chains, was shown to carry a binding affinity of 1 µM at CCR5 as an antagonist with potential anti-cancer activity. However, it is not drug-like according to the Lipinski's rule of five mainly due to its two long aliphatic side chains.

titre: Risks and Benefits of Bisphosphonate Therapies.
resume_court: Bisphosphonates are the mainstay of osteoporosis treatment but also play a fundamental role in treating other bone diseases such as Osteogenesis Imperfecta, Pagets' disease, and in the prevention of adverse skeletal effects in certain cancers such as prostate cancer or multiple myeloma. Other beneficial effects include pain reduction in bone metastasis and potentially a decrease in mortality.

titre: Circulating tumor cells are associated with poor overall survival in patients with cholangiocarcinoma.
resume_court: Circulating tumor cells (CTCs) in blood are associated with poor survival of patients with breast, prostate, or colon cancer. CTC =2 (HR, 10.5; 95% CI: 2.2-40.1; P < 0.01) and CTC =5 (HR, 10.2; 95% CI: 1.5-42.3; P = 0.02) were both associated with shorter survival among patients with perihilar/distal CCA. Assessment of CTCs may be useful for identifying CCA patients at risk of early mortality.

titre: Hyperactivated FRS2a-mediated signaling in prostate cancer cells promotes tumor angiogenesis and predicts poor clinical outcome of patients.
resume_court: Metastasis of tumors requires angiogenesis, which is comprised of multiple biological processes that are regulated by angiogenic factors. The fibroblast growth factor (FGF) is a potent angiogenic factor and aberrant FGF signaling is a common property of tumors. The results underscore the angiogenic role of FRS2a-mediated signaling in tumor epithelial cells in angiogenesis.

titre: Significance of urethral fibrosis evaluated by preoperative magnetic resonance imaging as a predictor of continence status after robot-assisted radical prostatectomy.
resume_court: The objective of this study was to assess the impact of urethral fibrosis on the continence status following robot-assisted radical prostatectomy (RARP). Furthermore, urethral fibrosis was identified as an independent predictor of the postoperative continence status at 3, 6, and 12?months after RARP. Copyright © 2015 John Wiley & Sons, Ltd.

titre: Giant Schmorl's Node may Cause High Uptake and Mimic a Bone Metastasis on (18)F-Choline Positron Emission Tomography/Computed Tomography.
resume_court: Bone metastasis in prostate cancer are detected by choline positron emission tomography/computed tomography (PET/CT) with high sensitivity and specificity. False positives on choline PET-CT caused by SN has not be reported in the literature and the present case highlights that this possibility should be considered in case of choline vertebral increased uptake in the patient with prostate cancer.

titre: Treatment of castration-resistant prostate cancer and bone metastases with radium-223 dichloride.
resume_court: Radium-223 dichloride (Ra-223) is the first a-particle emitting radiopharmaceutical to be approved for the treatment of patients with castration-resistant prostate cancer and associated bone metastases, and the first bone-targeting agent to significantly improve patient overall survival whilst reducing pain and the symptomatic skeletal events (SSEs) associated with bone metastases.

titre: Collagenous micronodules in prostate cancer revisited: are they solely associated with Gleason pattern 3 adenocarcinomas?
resume_court: Collagenous micronodules (CMs) are microscopic stromal nodular eosinophilic fibrillar collagen deposition of uncertain histogenesis seen in prostatic adenocarcinoma. This study suggests that CMs are more frequently associated with Gleason pattern 4 cancer warranting morphologic reappraisal of CMs, rather than the consensus assignment of Gleason pattern 3.

titre: Golgi phosphoprotein 3 regulates metastasis of prostate cancer via matrix metalloproteinase 9.
resume_court: Recent studies suggest that Golgi phosphoprotein 3 (GOLPH3) protein is a candidate metastasis gene in human cancer. The goal of this study was to determine the function of GOLPH3 in prostate cancer metastasis and to identify GOLPH3-regulated pathways and genes involved in prostate cancer metastasis. This regulation is probably mediated by EGFR and Src signaling pathways.

titre: A novel method to identify and isolate proliferative inflammatory atrophy (PIA) clusters and to extract high-quality PIA RNA.
resume_court: Epidemiological and histopathological studies have indicated that proliferative inflammatory atrophy (PIA) of the prostate is closely associated with the onset and development of prostate cancer (PCa). Therefore, the present study established a valid method to discover molecular evidence in support of the correlation between PIA and the development of PCa.

titre: Enhancement of performance in porous bead-based microchip sensors: Effects of chip geometry on bio-agent capture.
resume_court: Measuring low concentrations of clinically-important biomarkers using porous bead-based lab-on-a-chip (LOC) platforms is critical for the successful implementation of point-of-care (POC) devices. Such optimizations of the bead micro-container and bead geometries have the potential to significantly reduce the LODs and reagent costs for spatially programmed bead-based assay systems of this type.

titre: The Role of Osteoclasts in Early Dissemination of Prostate Cancer Tumor Cells.
resume_court: Prostate cancer (PCa) is one of the most common neoplasms that metastasize to bone. Before PCa injection, the number of TRAP+ OC was increased in mice treated with AMD3100, while treatment with BP resulted in relatively lower TRAP+ OCs. After PCa injection, however, the number of TRAP+ OCs was dramatically increased, but did not differ significantly amongst the treatment groups.

titre: The DAXX co-repressor is directly recruited to active regulatory elements genome-wide to regulate autophagy programs in a model of human prostate cancer.
resume_court: While carcinoma of the prostate is the second most common cause of cancer death in the US, current methods and markers used to predict prostate cancer (PCa) outcome are inadequate. DNMT1 and DAXX bound close to transcriptional activator motifs. Given DAXX's putative regulatory role in autophagy, future studies may consider DAXX as a candidate marker and therapeutic target for prostate cancer.

titre: Uncovering potential downstream targets of oncogenic GRPR overexpression in prostate carcinomas harboring ETS rearrangements.
resume_court: Gastrin-releasing peptide receptor (GRPR) is known to be overexpressed in several human malignancies, including prostate cancer, and has been implicated in multiple important neoplastic signaling pathways. Using an antibody microarray we were able to validate known and identify new targets of GRPR pathway, namely AKT1, PKCe, TYK2 and MST1.

titre: Prostate Cancer: Interobserver Agreement and Accuracy with the Revised Prostate Imaging Reporting and Data System at Multiparametric MR Imaging.
resume_court: To evaluate accuracy and interobserver variability with the use of the Prostate Imaging Reporting and Data System (PI-RADS) version 2.0 for detection of prostate cancer at multiparametric magnetic resonance (MR) imaging in a biopsy-naïve patient population. Use of the revised PI-RADS provides moderately reproducible MR imaging scores for detection of clinically relevant disease.

titre: Loss-of-function variants in ATM confer risk of gastric cancer.
resume_court: Gastric cancer is a serious health problem worldwide, with particularly high prevalence in eastern Asia. Genome-wide association studies (GWAS) in Asian populations have identified several loci that associate with gastric cancer risk. We found a new gastric cancer association with loss-of-function mutations in ATM (gene test, P = 8.0 × 10(-12); odds ratio (OR) = 4.74).

titre: Cardiovascular Risk Factors and Ethnicity Are Independent Factors Associated with Lower Urinary Tract Symptoms.
resume_court: To determine the lower urinary tract symptoms (LUTS) profile and factors affecting its degree of severity including cardiovascular risk profile, age, ethnicity, education level and prostate volume in a multiethnic Asian setting. The severity of LUTS was assessed using the International Prostate Symptom Score (IPSS). Severity of LUTS varies between different ethnicities across all age groups.

titre: Diagnosis of "Poorly Formed Glands" Gleason Pattern 4 Prostatic Adenocarcinoma on Needle Biopsy: An Interobserver Reproducibility Study Among Urologic Pathologists With Recommendations.
resume_court: Accurate recognition of Gleason pattern (GP) 4 prostate carcinoma (PCa) on needle biopsy is critical for patient management and prognostication. Grading "poorly formed glands" is challenging. This study represents an important step in standardization of grading of "poorly formed glands" based on quantitative and topographic morphologic features.

titre: Nuclear Brachyury Expression Is Consistent in Chordoma, Common in Germ Cell Tumors and Small Cell Carcinomas, and Rare in Other Carcinomas and Sarcomas: An Immunohistochemical Study of 5229 Cases.
resume_court: Brachyury is a transcription factor of the T-box family typically expressed in notochord and chordoma. Only nuclear labeling was scored, and antibody dilution of 1:2000 was used. Pulmonary small cell carcinoma was often positive (41%), whereas pulmonary and pancreatic adenocarcinomas only rarely showed nuclear brachyury positivity (3% to 4%).

titre: Early side effects and first results of radioligand therapy with (177)Lu-DKFZ-617 PSMA of castrate-resistant metastatic prostate cancer: a two-centre study.
resume_court: Radioligand therapy (RLT) with (177)Lu-DKFZ-617 PSMA (Lu-PSMA) (prostate-specific membrane antigen) is a novel targeted therapy of metastatic prostate cancer. (68)Ga-PSMA HBED-CC PET/CT was performed in all patients prior to RLT. A relevant PSA decline was detected in 70 % of patients.

titre: Cytotoxic triterpene saponins from Cercodemas anceps.
resume_court: Seven holostane-type triterpene saponins (1-7), including five new compounds namely cercodemasoides A-E (2-6), were isolated from the sea cucumber Cercodemas anceps. With respect to the potent cytotoxicity of the isolated saponins, further studies are required to confirm efficacy in vivo and the mechanism of cytotoxic effects.

titre: Novel Technique Prevents Lymphoceles After Transperitoneal Robotic-assisted Pelvic Lymph Node Dissection: Peritoneal Flap Interposition.
resume_court: To determine the efficacy of our novel technique to prevent lymphocele formation after pelvic lymph node dissection (PLND) after robotic-assisted radical prostatectomy (RARP) using the existing peritoneum of the bladder. Group A included the first 77 patients with PLND using standard technique (no peritoneal flap). Mean time to lymphocele detection in group A was 30.4 days.

titre: Baseline PSA in a Spanish male population aged 40-49 years anticipates detection of prostate cancer.
resume_court: We researched the usefulness of optimizing prostate cancer (PC) screening in our community using baseline PSA readings in men between 40-49 years of age. We compared the evolution of PSA from baseline in patients with consecutive readings using the Friedman test. The median baseline PSA was .74 (.01-58.5) ng/mL for patients without PC and 4.21 (.76-47.4) ng/mL for those with PC.

titre: Inhibition of microsomal prostaglandin E synthase-1 as targeted therapy in cancer treatment.
resume_court: The bioactive lipid prostaglandin E2 (PGE2) is involved in several steps of carcinogenesis in some of the most common cancers, e.g. colon cancer, lung cancer, prostate cancer and breast cancer. Non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) that target cyclooxygenase (COX) activity, the first step of the PGE2 biosynthesis, has been found to reduce the incidence of colon cancer.

titre: Visceral adipose tissue measured by computed tomography and high-grade prostate cancer after radical prostatectomy.
resume_court: We assessed the association between obesity measurements including visceral adipose tissue (VAT), measured by computed tomography, and the risk of high-grade prostate cancer after radical prostatectomy. BMI had different effects on GS depending on VAT. A higher BMI was associated with an increased risk of high-grade cancer only in patients with more VAT.

titre: Magnetic Resonance Imaging-Ultrasound Fusion Targeted Prostate Biopsy in a Consecutive Cohort of Men with No Previous Biopsy: Reduction of Over Detection through Improved Risk Stratification.
resume_court: MRF-TB (magnetic resonance imaging-ultrasound fusion targeted prostate biopsy) may improve the detection of prostate cancer in men presenting for prostate biopsy. We report clinical outcomes of 12-core systematic biopsy and MRF-TB in men who presented for primary biopsy and further describe pathological characteristics of cancers detected by systematic biopsy and not by MRF-TB.

titre: Survival and PSA-markers for mortality and metastasis in nonmetastatic prostate cancer treated with androgen deprivation therapy.
resume_court: Few studies have examined the risk of developing castration-resistant prostate cancer (CRPC), metastasis, and mortality among nonmetastatic prostate cancer (M0-PC) patients treated with androgen deprivation therapy (ADT). We estimated the incidence of these outcomes among M0-PC patients on ADT and identified prostate-specific antigen (PSA) based biomarkers for mortality and metastasis.

titre: Discovery and characterization of long intergenic non-coding RNAs (lincRNA) module biomarkers in prostate cancer: an integrative analysis of RNA-Seq data.
resume_court: Prostate cancer (PCa) is a leading cause of cancer-related death of men worldwide. Two modules (M3 and M5) were significantly enriched with lincRNAs, and one of them, M3, may be used as a lincRNA module-biomarker for PCa diagnosis. This study provides some important insights into the roles of lincRNAs in PCa and suggests a few lincRNAs as candidate biomarkers for PCa diagnosis and prognosis.

titre: Updated recommendations from the Spanish Oncology Genitourinary Group for the treatment of patients with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer.
resume_court: Prostate cancer is the most prevalent male urogenital malignancy. Approximately 30% of patients with prostate cancer will develop advanced disease. Due to the recent appearance of important new data and the complexity of decision-making in this field, SOGUG herein provides updated recommendations for the treatment of patients with metastatic prostate cancer.

titre: Real-time cancer diagnosis during prostate biopsy: ex vivo evaluation of full-field optical coherence tomography (FFOCT) imaging on biopsy cores.
resume_court: To evaluate the diagnostic accuracy (Acc) of full-field optical coherence tomography (FFOCT) for cancer detection on prostate biopsy. The overall average Acc was measured, as well as sensitivity (Se), specificity (Sp), positive and negative predictive values (PPV and NPV). The overall average Acc of FFOCT for cancer detection was of 70.6%.

titre: Androgen receptor aberrations in the era of abiraterone and enzalutamide.
resume_court: Prostate cancer is the most prevalent non-skin cancer and the second leading cause of cancer death in men of the western world. Although first-line androgen deprivation therapies like chemical/surgical castration and/or administration of anti-androgens are able to control the disease for several years, prostate cancer almost invariably recurs as castration-resistant prostate cancer.

titre: PSA bounce after ¹²5I-brachytherapy for prostate cancer as a favorable prognosticator.
resume_court: Permanent low-dose-rate brachytherapy (BT) with iodine 125 is an established curative treatment for localized prostate cancer. The median time to bounce was 12 months, the median time to biochemical failure was 30 months. In most cases, an early increase in PSA after BT indicates PSA bounce and is associated with a lower risk of biochemical failure.

titre: Dysregulated transcription across diverse cancer types reveals the importance of RNA-binding protein in carcinogenesis.
resume_court: It is well known that carcinogenesis is in part dictated by dysregulated transcription events and signal pathways. As we expected, the transcription of cancer-related genes was significantly deregulated in tumor vs. normal across all cancer types. Dysregulated transcription across cancer types reveals the importance of RBPs in carcinogenesis.

titre: Fisetin regulates TPA-induced breast cell invasion by suppressing matrix metalloproteinase-9 activation via the PKC/ROS/MAPK pathways.
resume_court: Invasion and metastasis are among the main causes of death in patients with malignant tumors. Our findings indicate the role of fisetin in MCF-7 cell invasion, and clarify the underlying molecular mechanisms of this role, suggesting fisetin as a potential chemopreventive agent for breast cancer metastasis.

titre: Pseudohyperplastic prostate carcinoma: histologic patterns and differential diagnosis.
resume_court: The similarity between some carcinomas and many benign glandular proliferations has been mentioned in the literature for decades. Other less frequent histologic varieties included adenosis-like pattern, prostatic intraepithelial neoplasia-like pattern, pseudohyperplastic adenocarcinoma with xanthomatous features, and limited pseudohyperplastic adenocarcinoma.

titre: Primary radiotherapy vs conservative management for localized prostate cancer--a population-based study.
resume_court: Radiotherapy is the most common curative cancer therapy used for elderly patients with localized prostate cancer. In patients with low-/intermediate-risk prostate cancer, 10-year prostate cancer-specific and overall survival was similar in high- and low-radiotherapy use areas (96.1 vs 95.4% and 56.6 vs 56.3%, respectively). Results were similar irrespective of the type of radiotherapy used.

titre: Treatment of mCRPC in the AR-axis-targeted therapy-resistant state.
resume_court: The increased use of the androgen receptor axis-targeted (ARAT) agents abiraterone and enzalutamide in first- and second-line treatment of metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC) has improved patient outcomes, but resistance to these agents is inevitable. Early identification of patients with primary or secondary resistance to ARAT therapy is of increasing clinical concern.

titre: Impact of polymorphisms of the DNA repair gene XRCC1 and their role in the risk of prostate cancer.
resume_court: We conducted a case-control study to examine the role of XRCC1 codons 194 (Arg>Trp), 280 (Arg>His) and 399 (Arg>Gln) polymorphisms in the risk of prostate cancer. We did not find significant association between XRCC1 194 (Arg>Trp) polymorphism and clinical stage and Gleason score of prostate cancer (P>0.05).

titre: Quality of life in patients with prostate cancer: validation of an instrument for clinical practice.
resume_court: The objective of this work is to validate a Spanish version of the EPIC-CP. For reliability evaluation, the Cronbach's alpha was used to test the internal consistency for each domain of the EPIC-CP. The Spanish version of the EPIC-CP is reliable and valid, so it is a useful tool to measure the quality of life in patients with prostate cancer, as well as the impact of different treatments.

titre: Expression of P504S and matrix metalloproteinase-2 in circulating prostate cells disseminated as a result of transrectal ultrasound guided biopsy as determined by immunocytochemistry: Clinical implications.
resume_court: Surgical manipulation of cancer has been shown to increase blood borne cancer cell dissemination and increase the risk of metastasis. 13/14 had P504S (+) and MMP-2 (+) cells detected prior to biopsy. In cancer negative men, P504S (-) and MMP-2 (-) cells were detected, some of these cells persisted 24 hours after biopsy.

titre: Semiparametric estimation in the proportional hazard model accounting for a misclassified cause of failure.
resume_court: Misclassified causes of failures are a common phenomenon in competing risks survival data such as cancer mortality. We propose new estimating equations for a semiparametric proportional hazards (PH) model with misattributed causes of failures. The methods are applied to analyze prostate cancer survival.

titre: Location of Prostate Cancers Determined by Multiparametric and MRI-Guided Biopsy in Patients With Elevated Prostate-Specific Antigen Level and at Least One Negative Transrectal Ultrasound-Guided Biopsy.
resume_court: Cancers with a maximum cancer core length of 6 mm or more were more likely to be located in the anterior part of the prostate than were cancers with a core length of less than 6 mm (66% vs 6%). Anterior involvement was high (76%) in patients with an elevated PSA level and one or more negative TRUS-guided biopsy session, and the majority of these cancers (93%) were intermediate or high risk.

titre: Feasibility Study of 3-T DWI of the Prostate: Readout-Segmented Versus Single-Shot Echo-Planar Imaging.
resume_court: The mean Likert scores for standard ss-EPI and rs-EPI were as follows: image sharpness, 2.9 and 4.6; distortion level, 2.8 and 4.4; contrast, 3.1 and 3.8; lesion conspicuity, 3.0 and 4.0; structure, 3.1 and 4.2; and overall image quality, 3.1 and 4.2. The rs-EPI DWI sequence was associated with significantly better image quality and fewer susceptibility artifacts than was ss-EPI (all p < 0.05).

titre: Diagnosis of Extracapsular Extension of Prostate Cancer on Prostate MRI: Impact of Second-Opinion Readings by Subspecialized Genitourinary Oncologic Radiologists.
resume_court: The purpose of this article is to investigate the added value of second-opinion evaluation of prostate MRI by subspecialized genitourinary oncologic radiologists for the assessment of extracapsular extension (ECE) of prostate cancer. On ROC curve analysis, the second-opinion reports yielded a statistically significantly higher AUC for the detection of ECE (0.80 vs 0.65; p = 0.004).

titre: Characteristics of Detected and Missed Prostate Cancer Foci on 3-T Multiparametric MRI Using an Endorectal Coil Correlated With Whole-Mount Thin-Section Histopathology.
resume_court: The objective of this study was to determine the characteristics of prostate cancer foci missed on 3-T multiparametric MRI performed with an endorectal coil. Of the 285 cancer foci detected at histopathology, 153 (53.3%) were missed on MRI and 132 (46.7%) were detected on MRI. Of the missed lesions, 75.2% were low-grade prostate cancer.

titre: Investigation on the performance of dedicated radiotherapy positioning devices for MR scanning for prostate planning.
resume_court: The purpose of this study was to investigate performance of the couch and coil mounts designed for MR-simulation prostate scanning using data from ten volunteers. They also were scanned using a MR-simulation table top and pelvic coil mounts. The image signal was reduced after applying the coil mount, but no significant effect was found on prostate contouring.

titre: Accelerated tomotherapy delivery with TomoEdge technique.
resume_court: TomoEDGE is an advanced delivery form of tomotherapy which uses a dynamic secondary collimator. If, after analysis in terms of beam on time, integral dose, dose conformity, and organ at risk sparing the treating physician decided that the Edge 5 plan was not suitable for clinical treatment, a plan with TomoEdge and 2.5 cm field width was created (Edge 2.5) and used for the treatment.

titre: Intrafractional prostate motion during external beam radiotherapy monitored by a real-time target localization system.
resume_court: This paper investigates the clinical significance of real-time monitoring of intrafractional prostate motion during external beam radiotherapy using a commercial 4D localization system. The percentage of tracking time during which the prostate shifted > 2, 3, 5, and 7 mm was 27.8%, 10.7%, 1.6%, and 0.3%, respectively, and it was 56.2%, 33.7%, 11.2%, and 2.1%, respectively, for the ten patients.

titre: Dosimetric validation and clinical implementation of two 3D dose verification systems for quality assurance in volumetric-modulated arc therapy techniques.
resume_court: A pretreatment quality assurance program for volumetric techniques should include redundant calculations and measurement-based verifications. Comparisons between measurements taken with a 2D ion chamber array and results obtained by both systems for real VMAT plans were also performed (mean global gamma passing rates better than 87.0% and 97.9% for the 2%/2 mm and 3%/3 mm criteria).

titre: Evaluation of a single-scan protocol for radiochromic film dosimetry.
resume_court: The purpose of this study was to evaluate a single-scan protocol using Gafchromic EBT3 film (EBT3) by comparing it with the commonly used 24-hr measurement protocol for radiochromic film dosimetry. The dose distribution for the single-scan protocol was within 2% of the 24-hr protocol dose distribution. The pass rates were 96.0% for the single-scan protocol and 95.9% for the 24-hr protocol.

titre: Potential of 3D printing technologies for fabrication of electron bolus and proton compensators.
resume_court: This study investigated the potential of utilizing 3D printing technologies for the fabrication of the electron bolus and proton compensators. The HU of the printed electron bolus was 106.5 ± 15.2. The profiles of the electron bolus and proton compensator were compared with the original designs.

titre: In vivo endorectal dosimetry of prostate tomotherapy using dual MOSkin detectors.
resume_court: Verification of dose to the anterior rectal wall in helical tomotherapy to the prostate is important due to the close proximity of the rectal wall to the treatment field. The steep dose gradient makes these measurements challenging. Despite the very high-dose gradient region, real-time measurements of the anterior rectal wall doses were within acceptable limits of TPS-predicted doses.

titre: Evaluation of patient DVH-based QA metrics for prostate VMAT: correlation between accuracy of estimated 3D patient dose and magnitude of MLC misalignment.
resume_court: The purpose of this study was to evaluate the accuracy of commercially available software, using patient DVH-based QA metrics, by investigating the correlation between estimated 3D patient dose and magnitude of MLC misalignments. We calculated the dose differences between the ACPDP dose with error and TPS dose with error using gamma passing rates and using DVH-based QA metrics.

titre: Volumetric-modulated arc therapy planning using multicriteria optimization for localized prostate cancer.
resume_court: The purpose of this work is to evaluate the volumetric-modulated arc therapy (VMAT) multicriteria optimization (MCO) algorithm clinically available in the RayStation treatment planning system (TPS) and its ability to reduce treatment planning time while providing high dosimetric plan quality.

titre: A Web application for the management of clinical workflow in image-guided and adaptive proton therapy for prostate cancer treatments.
resume_court: Image-guided radiotherapy (IGRT), based on radiopaque markers placed in the prostate gland, was used for proton therapy of prostate patients. Data models included patients, staff, treatment fields and records, correction vectors, DIPS images, and association logics. The system effectively modeled the clinical workflow and IGRT process.

titre: Validation of an RNA cell cycle progression score for predicting death from prostate cancer in a conservatively managed needle biopsy cohort.
resume_court: The natural history of prostate cancer is highly variable and difficult to predict accurately. The primary end point was prostate cancer death. The CCP score provides significant pretreatment prognostic information that cannot be provided by clinical variables and is useful for determining which patients can be safely managed conservatively, avoiding radical treatment.

titre: Dual inhibition of survivin and MAOA synergistically impairs growth of PTEN-negative prostate cancer.
resume_court: Survivin and monoamine oxidase A (MAOA) levels are elevated in prostate cancer (PCa) compared to normal prostate glands. However, the relationship between survivin and MAOA in PCa is unclear. Survivin depletion delayed MAOA increase during PCa progression, and silencing MAOA decreased survivin expression.

titre: Grb2 monomer-dimer equilibrium determines normal versus oncogenic function.
resume_court: The adaptor protein growth factor receptor-bound protein 2 (Grb2) is ubiquitously expressed in eukaryotic cells and involved in a multitude of intracellular protein interactions. Grb2 exists in a constitutive equilibrium between monomeric and dimeric states. The self-association/dissociation of Grb2 represents a switch that regulates MAP kinase activity and hence controls cancer progression.

titre: Noncoplanar Beam Angle Class Solutions to Replace Time-Consuming Patient-Specific Beam Angle Optimization in Robotic Prostate Stereotactic Body Radiation Therapy.
resume_court: To investigate development of a recipe for the creation of a beam angle class solution (CS) for noncoplanar prostate stereotactic body radiation therapy to replace time-consuming individualized beam angle selection (iBAS) without significant loss in plan quality, using the in-house "Erasmus-iCycle" optimizer for fully automated beam profile optimization and iBAS.

titre: Importance of Local Control in Early-Stage Prostate Cancer: Outcomes of Patients With Positive Post-Radiation Therapy Biopsy Results Treated in RTOG 9408.
resume_court: The purpose of this study was to assess the association between positive post-radiation therapy (RT) biopsy results and subsequent clinical outcomes in males with localized prostate cancer. A total of 831 patients underwent post-RT biopsy, 398 were treated with RT alone and 433 with RT plus TAS.

titre: Consensus Guidelines and Contouring Atlas for Pelvic Node Delineation in Prostate and Pelvic Node Intensity Modulated Radiation Therapy.
resume_court: In total, 84 nodal contours were evaluated. LN coverage was similar in all groups, with all of the vascular-expansion techniques (RTOG, modified RTOG, and PIVOTAL), resulting in larger CTVs than that of the RMH technique (mean volumes: 287.3 cm(3), 326.7 cm(3), 310.3 cm(3), and 256.7 cm(3), respectively). Vascular expansion techniques result in larger LN-CTVs than the freehand RMH technique.

titre: Defining the "Hostile Pelvis" for Intensity Modulated Radiation Therapy: The Impact of Anatomic Variations in Pelvic Dimensions on Dose Delivered to Target Volumes and Organs at Risk in Patients With High-Risk Prostate Cancer Treated With Whole Pelvic Radiation Therapy.
resume_court: The aim of this study was to evaluate the impact of variations in pelvic dimensions on the dose delivered to the target volumes and the organs at risk (OARs) in patients with high-risk prostate cancer (PCa) to be treated with whole pelvic radiation therapy (WPRT) in an attempt to define the hostile pelvis in terms of intensity modulated radiation therapy (IMRT).

titre: Post-treated prostate cancer: normal findings and signs of local relapse on multiparametric magnetic resonance imaging.
resume_court: The use of multiparametric magnetic resonance imaging (mp-MRI) for prostate cancer has increased over recent years, mainly for detection, staging, and active surveillance. The authors provide a pictorial review of the normal findings and the signs of local tumor relapse after radical prostatectomy, external beam radiotherapy, brachytherapy, cryosurgery, and hormonal therapy.

titre: The impact of low-dose carcinogens and environmental disruptors on tissue invasion and metastasis.
resume_court: The purpose of this review is to stimulate new ideas regarding low-dose environmental mixtures and carcinogens and their potential to promote invasion and metastasis. This we hope will lead to the collaboration between scientists who have dedicated their professional life to the study of carcinogens and those whose interests are exclusively in the arena of tissue invasion and metastasis.

titre: Assessing the carcinogenic potential of low-dose exposures to chemical mixtures in the environment: the challenge ahead.
resume_court: Only 15% (13/85) were found to have evidence of a dose-response threshold, whereas 59% (50/85) exerted low-dose effects. No dose-response information was found for the remaining 26% (22/85). Additional basic research on carcinogenesis and research focused on low-dose effects of chemical mixtures needs to be rigorously pursued before the merits of this hypothesis can be further advanced.

titre: Bony non-union in a patient receiving androgen deprivation therapy for prostate cancer.
resume_court: We present a case of a 76-year-old man who underwent a corrective femoral osteotomy for a varus deformity and stress fractures. Orthopaedic surgeons treating fractures in this patient population need to aware of the problems associated with ADT and closely liaise with oncologists and urologists to stop ADT or start alternative treatment until bony union has been achieved.

titre: Similarity of Serum and Plasma Insulin-like Growth Factor Concentrations.
resume_court: Insulin-like growth factors (IGFs) are implicated in many normal physiological processes and pathological states, including cancer. This study aimed to compare IGFs in matched serum and plasma samples. Concordance correlation coefficients of matched serum/plasma specimens were 0.92, 0.91, 0.82, 0.96, and 0.99 for IGF-I, IGFBP-3, IGF-II, C-peptide, and leptin, respectively.

titre: A New Combinatorial Optimization Approach for Integrated Feature Selection Using Different Datasets: A Prostate Cancer Transcriptomic Study.
resume_court: The joint study of multiple datasets has become a common technique for increasing statistical power in detecting biomarkers obtained from smaller studies. We propose a new combinatorial optimization problem that addresses the core issue of biomarker detection in integrated datasets. The model we propose is a generalised version of the (a,ß)-k-Feature Set problem.

titre: Association between MTHFR C677T Polymorphism and Risk of Prostate Cancer: Evidence from 22 Studies with 10,832 Cases and 11,993 Controls.
resume_court: The MTHFR C677T polymorphism is a genetic alteration affecting an enzyme involved in folate metabolism, but its relationship to host susceptibility to prostate cancer remains uncertain. Meta-analysis showed that there was no obvious association between MTHFR C677T polymorphism and risk of prostate cancer under all five genetic models.

titre: Intermittent Androgen Suppression: Estimating Parameters for Individual Patients Based on Initial PSA Data in Response to Androgen Deprivation Therapy.
resume_court: When a physician decides on a treatment and its schedule for a specific patient, information gained from prior patients and experience in the past is taken into account. Although we used data from prostate cancer patients, the proposed method is general, and thus can be applied to other diseases once an appropriate mathematical model is established for that disease.

titre: Deregulation of MiR-34b/Sox2 Predicts Prostate Cancer Progression.
resume_court: Most men diagnosed with prostate cancer will have an indolent and curable disease, whereas approximately 15% of these patients will rapidly progress to a castrate-resistant and metastatic stage with high morbidity and mortality. In turn, loss of miR-34b resulted in downstream deregulation and overexpression of the "stemness" marker, Sox2.

titre: Rheumatoid Arthritis as a Therapeutic Challenge in a Patient with Lynch Syndrome.
resume_court: Lynch syndrome (LS) is an inherited colorectal cancer (CRC) syndrome accounting for about 3-5% of all cases and involves significantly higher risk of subsequent malignancies, colonic as well as extra-colonic. Our case demonstrates the development of CRC, endometrial cancer, and breast cancer as a presentation of LS in a patient with RA and presents a therapeutic challenge for RA treatment.

titre: Evaluation of hGM-CSF/hTNFa surface-modified prostate cancer therapeutic vaccine in the huPBL-SCID chimeric mouse model.
resume_court: To validate its efficacy in the context of the human immune system, a novel therapeutic vaccine of hGM-CSF/hTNFa surface-modified PC-3 cells against human prostate cancer was evaluated in the human peripheral blood lymphocytes-severe combined immunodeficiency (huPBL-SCID) chimeric mouse model.

titre: Multiplex pyrosequencing assay using AdvISER-MH-PYRO algorithm: a case for rapid and cost-effective genotyping analysis of prostate cancer risk-associated SNPs.
resume_court: Single Nucleotide Polymorphisms (SNPs) identified in Genome Wide Association Studies (GWAS) have generally moderate association with related complex diseases. In the current study, two multiplex assays were developed consisting of a quadruplex (n=4) and a quintuplex (n=5) polymerase chain reaction (PCR) each followed by multiplex pyrosequencing analysis.

titre: The HOXB13 G84E Mutation Is Associated with an Increased Risk for Prostate Cancer and Other Malignancies.
resume_court: A rare nonconservative substitution (G84E) in the HOXB13 gene has been shown to be associated with risk of prostate cancer. However, the mutation was also more commonly observed in men with bladder cancer (P = 0.06) and leukemia (P = 0.01). The associations between HOXB13 and prostate, leukemia, and bladder suggest that this gene is important in carcinogenesis.

titre: Androgen Receptor Targeted Conjugate for Bimodal Photodynamic Therapy of Prostate Cancer in Vitro.
resume_court: Prostate cancer (PC) represents the most common type of cancer among males and is the second leading cause of cancer death in men in Western society. Overall, the presented approach is very promising for further development of AR-photosensitizer conjugates in the multimodal photodynamic treatment of prostate cancer.

titre: Prostatitis, other genitourinary infections and prostate cancer: results from a population-based case-control study.
resume_court: We relied on a population-based case-control study (PROtEuS) to examine a potential association between the presence of histologically confirmed prostate cancer (PCa) and history of genitourinary infections, e.g., prostatitis, urethritis, orchitis and epididymitis. Cases were 1933 men with incident PCa, diagnosed across Montreal hospitals between 2005 and 2009.

titre: Sirolimus effects on cancer incidence after kidney transplantation: a meta-analysis.
resume_court: Sirolimus, an immunosuppressant option for kidney transplant recipients, may reduce cancer risk by interrupting the mammalian target of rapamycin pathway. However, sirolimus use had associations with lower kidney cancer incidence (IRR = 0.40, 95% CI = 0.20-0.81), and higher prostate cancer incidence (IRR = 1.85, 95% CI = 1.17-2.91).

titre: Analysis of autophagic flux in response to sulforaphane in metastatic prostate cancer cells.
resume_court: The phytochemical sulforaphane (SF) has been shown to decrease prostate cancer metastases in a genetic mouse model of prostate carcinogenesis, though the mechanism of action is not fully known. We found that SF can stimulate autophagic flux and cell death only at high concentrations, above what has been observed in vivo.

titre: Positron-emission tomography in urooncology
resume_court: The use of positron emission tomography (PET) is an established method for the diagnosis of urological malignancies. While (18)F-FDG-PET is recognized in current guidelines for the staging of seminoma, PET is not used in clinical routine in renal malignancies due to the lack of specific tracers. Here, (68)Ga-PSMA-PET might be included in the future as part of standard imaging work-up.

titre: A profile of enzalutamide for the treatment of advanced castration resistant prostate cancer.
resume_court: Recent advances in understanding the mechanisms underlying the development and progression of castration resistant prostate cancer from androgen-sensitive prostate cancer have provided new avenues exploring efficacious therapies in a disease which is the second leading cause of cancer deaths among men in the western world.

titre: Volumetric modulated arc therapy in prostate cancer patients with metallic hip prostheses in a UK centre.
resume_court: This study aimed to investigate whether IMRT using VMAT is a viable and safe solution in dose escalated RT in these patients. 20/23 plans met all OAR constraints (rectum, bladder). VMAT provides an elegant solution to deliver dose escalated RT in patients with unilateral and bilateral hip replacements with minimal acute and late toxicities.

titre: Circulating Long Noncoding RNA as a Potential Target for Prostate Cancer.
resume_court: Prostate cancer is considered the second most common visceral malignancy in men in Western countries. This review focuses mainly on literature evidence for the role of long noncoding RNA in prostate cancer, which may suggest novel strategies for its prognosis, diagnosis and clinical treatment.

titre: Identifying in vivo DCE MRI markers associated with microvessel architecture and gleason grades of prostate cancer.
resume_court: To identify computer extracted in vivo dynamic contrast enhanced (DCE) MRI markers associated with quantitative histomorphometric (QH) characteristics of microvessels and Gleason scores (GS) in prostate cancer. Computer extracted features of prostate DCE MRI appear to be correlated with microvessel architecture and may be discriminative of low versus intermediate and high GS.

titre: By inhibiting snail signaling and miR-23a-3p, osthole suppresses the EMT-mediated metastatic ability in prostate cancer.
resume_court: Osthole inhibited the TGF-ß/Akt/MAPK pathways, reduced Snail-DNA-binding activity and induced E-cadherin. We found that osthole decreased miR-23a-3p. Ectopic miR-23a-3p suppressed E-cadherin 3' untranslated region reporter activity and E-cadherin expression, and relieved the motility suppression caused by osthole treatment.

titre: Enrichment of the Cancer Stem Phenotype in Sphere Cultures of Prostate Cancer Cell Lines Occurs through Activation of Developmental Pathways Mediated by the Transcriptional Regulator ?Np63a.
resume_court: Cancer stem cells (CSC) drive prostate cancer tumor survival and metastasis. Suspension culture systems have been reported to enrich CSCs in primary cultures and cell lines. This platform can be readily adapted to enrich and assay actual patient samples, in order to design patient-specific therapies that are aimed particularly against CSCs.

titre: Changes in Epithelium, Stroma, and Lumen Space Correlate More Strongly with Gleason Pattern and Are Stronger Predictors of Prostate ADC Changes than Cellularity Metrics.
resume_court: There was a stronger correlation of Gleason pattern with gland component volumes (n = 553) of epithelium (Spearman ? = 0.898, P < .001), stroma (? = -0.651, P < .001), and lumen space (? = -0.912, P = .007) than with the cellularity metrics (n = 288) nuclear area (? = 0.422, P = .133) or nuclear count (? = 0.082, P = .780).

titre: Trends in cancer incidence in Maputo, Mozambique, 1991-2008.
resume_court: Very limited information is available regarding the incidence of cancer in sub-Saharan Africa. We analyzed changes in cancer patterns from 1991 to 2008 in Maputo (Mozambique). Prostate cancer showed the most dramatic increase over the whole study period (AAPC +11.3%; 95% CI: 9.7-13.0), with an ASR of 61.7 per 105 in 2003-2008.

titre: Geographic analysis of urologist density and prostate cancer mortality in the United States.
resume_court: Financial and demographic pressures in US require an understanding of the most efficient distribution of physicians to maximize population-level health benefits. In contrast, the urologist density was not significantly associated with the prostate state mortality in the new England region. The strength of association between urologist density and prostate cancer mortality varied regionally.

titre: Why do men suffering from LUTS seek primary medical care? A qualitative study.
resume_court: Lower urinary tract symptoms (LUTS) are common problems among men, but only a small proportion actually visit their general practitioner (GP). The main reasons to seek primary medical care are the need for reassurance and the nuisance of symptoms, especially nycturia. Overall, the patients show remarkably poor knowledge about their symptoms.

titre: Randomized phase II trial of docetaxel with or without PSA-TRICOM vaccine in patients with castrate-resistant metastatic prostate cancer: A trial of the ECOG-ACRIN cancer research group (E1809).
resume_court: Anti-tumor vaccines have demonstrated efficacy in patients with castration-resistant metastatic prostate cancer. The current trial was planned to assess the clinical efficacy of this vaccine in patients with castration-resistant metastatic prostate cancer receiving subsequent docetaxel chemotherapy. The primary endpoint of overall survival cannot be assessed due to limited accrual.

titre: In-bore prostate transperineal interventions with an MRI-guided parallel manipulator: system development and preliminary evaluation.
resume_court: Robot-assisted minimally-invasive surgery is well recognized as a feasible solution for diagnosis and treatment of prostate cancer in humans. This paper discusses the kinematics of a parallel 4 Degrees-of-Freedom (DOF) surgical manipulator designed for minimally invasive in-bore prostate percutaneous interventions through the patient's perineum. Copyright © 2015 John Wiley & Sons, Ltd.

titre: Prostate Cancer Metastases to Inguinal Lymph Nodes Detected by Attenuation-Corrected 11C-Acetate PET/CT.
resume_court: The inguinal lymph nodes are an unusual site of metastases for prostate adenocarcinoma. The attenuation-corrected CT portion of the scan also showed anterior wall thickening of the rectum. The imaging findings were suggestive of metastatic involvement of the rectum below the dentate line with subsequent spread to the inguinal lymph nodes.

titre: Relationship Between Prebiopsy Multiparametric Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI), Biopsy Indication, and MRI-ultrasound Fusion-targeted Prostate Biopsy Outcomes.
resume_court: Increasing evidence supports the use of magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)-ultrasound fusion-targeted prostate biopsy (MRF-TB) to improve the detection of clinically significant prostate cancer (PCa) while limiting detection of indolent disease compared to systematic 12-core biopsy (SB). To compare MRF-TB and SB results and investigate the relationship between biopsy outcomes and prebiopsy MRI.

titre: In Vivo Cancer Dual-Targeting and Dual-Modality Imaging with Functionalized Quantum Dots.
resume_court: Semiconductor quantum dots (QDs), after surface modification to provide water solubility and biocompatibility, have a promising future in biomedical applications. In vivo dual-modality PET/NIRF imaging of prostate tumor-bearing mice was investigated using QD-RGD-BBN and 2-(18)F-fluoropropionyl-QD-RGD-BBN ((18)F-FP-QD-RGD-BBN).

titre: Prospective Comparison of 18F-Fluoromethylcholine Versus 68Ga-PSMA PET/CT in Prostate Cancer Patients Who Have Rising PSA After Curative Treatment and Are Being Considered for Targeted Therapy.
resume_court: In prostate cancer with biochemical failure after therapy, current imaging techniques have a low detection rate at the prostate-specific antigen (PSA) levels at which targeted salvage therapy is effective. In patients with biochemical failure and a low PSA level, (68)Ga-PSMA demonstrated a significantly higher detection rate than (18)F-fluoromethylcholine and a high overall impact on management.

titre: Assessment of association between genetic variants in microRNA genes hsa-miR-499, hsa-miR-196a2 and hsa-miR-27a and prostate cancer risk in Serbian population.
resume_court: Due to their potentially functional significance, genetic variants within microRNA genes have been recognized as candidates for cancer-related genetic biomarkers. Furthermore, our study provided the first evidence of association between rs895819 and PCa risk, as well as for its genetic association with the presence of distant metastases among PCa patients.

titre: A Family History of Lethal Prostate Cancer and Risk of Aggressive Prostate Cancer in Patients Undergoing Radical Prostatectomy.
resume_court: We investigated whether a family history of lethal prostate cancer (PCa) was associated with high-risk disease or biochemical recurrence in patients undergoing radical prostatectomy. A cohort of radical prostatectomy patients was stratified into men with no family history of PCa (NFH); a first-degree relative with PCa (FH); and those with a first-degree relative who had died of PCa (FHD).

titre: A pilot randomised controlled trial of personalised care after treatment for prostate cancer (TOPCAT-P): nurse-led holistic-needs assessment and individualised psychoeducational intervention: study protocol.
resume_court: Prostate cancer is common and the incidence is increasing, but more men are living longer after diagnosis, and die with their disease rather than of it. We will recruit 120 patients who will be randomised to receive either an augmented form of usual care, or an additional nurse-led intervention for a period of 36 weeks. Healthcare service use will be measured over 36 weeks.

titre: Salvage brachytherapy for locally recurrent prostate cancer after external beam radiotherapy.
resume_court: External beam radiotherapy (EBRT) is a standard treatment for prostate cancer. However, few studies have examined the use of brachytherapy to treat post-EBRT recurrent prostate cancer. The purpose of this paper is to analyze the current state of our knowledge about the effects of salvage brachytherapy in patients who develop locally recurrent prostate cancer after primary EBRT.

titre: New therapies for relapsed castration-resistant prostate cancer based on peptide analogs of hypothalamic hormones.
resume_court: It is a pleasure to contribute our presentation at the International Prostate Forum of the Annual Meeting of the American Urological Association (AUA) to this special issue of the Asian Journal of Andrology.

titre: Hormone naïve prostate cancer: predicting and maximizing response intervals.
resume_court: Hormone naïve advanced prostate cancer is subdivided into two disease states: biochemical recurrence and traditional M1 (metastatic) prostate cancer and characterized by no prior hormonal therapy or androgen deprivation therapy (ADT). On the other hand, in the setting of M1 hormone naïve prostate cancer, there are many more RCT's to inform our decisions.

titre: Preventing aggressive prostate cancer with proven cardiovascular disease preventive methods.
resume_court: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) has been the number one cause of death in the U.S. for 114 of the last 115 years. Risk factors for prostate cancer have primarily mirrored risk proven risk factors for CVD, especially aggressive disease. The evidence also suggests proven CVD preventive measures are identical to prostate cancer preventive measures, especially in regard to aggressive disease.

titre: External beam radiotherapy for localized prostate cancer.
resume_court: Radiotherapy (XRT) is a curative treatment option for prostate cancer (PCa). The aim of this paper is to review the current literature and guidelines on external beam radiation therapy for PCa. However, brachytherapy and radiosurgery, a recently evolving relatively new technology for the radiotherapeutic management of localized PCa, are beyond the scope of this paper.

titre: Assessment of gold nanoparticle effect on prostate cancer LNCaP cells.
resume_court: In recent years gold nanoparticles (AuNPs) have received considerable attention for various biomedical applications including diagnostics and targeted drug delivery. Given absence of morphological changes in live cells and dribble and relatively constant numbers of dead cells, it was concluded that inhibitory effect of AuNPs on LNCaP cells growth was caused by alterations of proliferation.

titre: Survival rates of familial and sporadic prostate cancer patients.
resume_court: To compare cancer-specific survival rates for familial and sporadic prostate cancer patients. Comparing Gleason score between familial group and sporadic group revealed no statistically significant difference. The study data demonstrate statistically significant difference between familial group and sporadic group concerning age and cancer-specific survival rates, but not Gleason score.

titre: Expression and significance of cortactin and HDAC6 in human prostatic foamy gland carcinoma.
resume_court: Cortactin, the cytoplasmic substrate of HDAC6, is known to play an actin cytoskeletal regulatory role which is implicated in the motility of cancer cells, and thus in cancer progression. In this study, we aimed to identify the expression and potential role of cortactin and HDAC6 in PfCa. Cortactin and HDAC6 were associated with poor prognosis of patients with PfCa (P < 0.05).

titre: Diagnostic Value of Different Systematic Prostate Biopsy Methods in the Detection of Prostate Cancer with Ultrasonographic Hypoechoic Lesions--A Comparative Study.
resume_court: To assess if a less extended biopsy in the transperineal approach is sufficient for detection of prostate cancer (PC) in patients with hypoechoic lesions. PC was detected in 64.1% (107/167) of patients. A more limited biopsy scheme could be sufficient for the detection of PC if the hypoechoic lesion is sampled.

titre: Testosterone in the management of metastatic prostate cancer
resume_court: Background Among all cancer types, prostate cancer (PCa) is the most prevalent cancer and is the third-leading cause of cancer-related death in men. For many years, the androgen hypothesis had been accepted to explain the correlation between testosterone levels and the development or progression of PCa. There is growing evidence suggesting a prognostic role of testosterone levels in mCRPC.

titre: mPGES-1 in prostate cancer controls stemness and amplifies epidermal growth factor receptor-driven oncogenicity.
resume_court: There is evidence that an inflammatory microenvironment is associated with the development and progression of prostate cancer (PCa), although the determinants of intrinsic inflammation in PCa cells are not completely understood. Although EGFR inhibition reduces mPGES-1(SC) and mPGES-1(KD) cell xenograft tumour growth, we show that mPGES-1/PGE2 signalling sensitizes tumour cells to EGFR inhibitors.

titre: Current perspectives on FOXA1 regulation of androgen receptor signaling and prostate cancer.
resume_court: FOXA1 (also known as hepatocyte nuclear factor 3a, or HNF-3a) is a protein of the FKHD family transcription factors. In this review, we discuss our current understanding of FOXA1 regulation of prostatic and non-prostatic AR-chromatin targeting.

titre: Prostate Imaging--An Update.
resume_court: New technical and clinical developments of sonography and magnetic resonance imaging include improved detection, localization and staging as well as active surveillance of prostate cancer. The new PI-RADS Version 2 claims to eliminate the limitations of PI-RADS Version 1 and to allow globally recognized standardized diagnostic reporting.

titre: AIM2 Drives Joint Inflammation in a Self-DNA Triggered Model of Chronic Polyarthritis.
resume_court: Mice lacking DNase II display a polyarthritis-like disease phenotype that is driven by translocation of self-DNA into the cytoplasm of phagocytic cells, where it is sensed by pattern recognition receptors. To this end, we studied the role of the DNA-sensing inflammasome receptor AIM2 in this self-DNA driven disease model.

titre: Fried food and prostate cancer risk: systematic review and meta-analysis.
resume_court: We performed systematic review and meta-analysis of published studies that investigated the potential association between fried food consumption and prostate cancer risk. The results of this systematic literature review support the notion that larger intake of fried foods may have a role in increasing the risk of prostate cancer.

titre: Poly-Electrophilic Sesquiterpene Lactones from Vernonia amygdalina: New Members and Differences in Their Mechanism of Thiol Trapping and in Bioactivity.
resume_court: In addition to known compounds, the leaves of Vernonia amygdalina afforded the new sesquiterpene lactones 14-O-methylvernolide (2), 3'-deoxyvernodalol (6), and vernomygdalin (8). The exomethylene lactones are characterized by multiple Michael acceptor sites, as exemplified by vernolide (1) and vernodalol (5).

titre: Skeletal Metastasis of Unknown Primary Origin at the Initial Visit: A Retrospective Analysis of 286 Cases.
resume_court: Skeletal metastasis is a common metastatic event for several carcinomas, and the treatment for skeletal metastasis of unknown primary (SMUP) are a critical issue in cancer therapy. The median survival time of the SMUP patients was 20.0 months, while the median survival times of solitary bone metastasis cases and multi-bone metastasis cases were 39.0 months and 16.0 months, respectively.

titre: Hibiscus sabdariffa Leaf Extract Inhibits Human Prostate Cancer Cell Invasion via Down-Regulation of Akt/NF-kB/MMP-9 Pathway.
resume_court: Hibiscus sabdariffa leaf has been previously shown to possess hypoglycemic, hypolipidemic, and antioxidant effects, and induce tumor cell apoptosis. These findings suggested that the inhibition of MMP-9 expression by HLE may act through the suppression of the Akt/NF-kB signaling pathway, which in turn led to the reduced invasiveness of the cancer cells.

titre: Two-Port Approach Compared to Standard Laparoscopic Radical Cystectomy.
resume_court: Two-port laparoscopic radical cystectomy (LRC) using a multichannel platform through the umbilicus and one additional 10-mm in the right iliac fossa has been recently described. A matched-pair study comparing perioperative outcomes, postoperative visual analog pain scale (VAPS), and morbidity of two-port (n=30) and four-port (n=30) LRC. Length of hospital stay was also equivalent.

titre: Preclinical imaging of kallikrein-related peptidase 2 (hK2) in prostate cancer with a (111)In-radiolabelled monoclonal antibody, 11B6.
resume_court: Prostate cancer is a leading cause of death in the male population of the western world. SPECT/CT imaging of subcutaneous and intra-tibial LNCaP xenografts was used to visualize the tumours. Tumour uptake of (111)In-DTPA-11B6 in LNCaP xenografts was 19%?±?0.78%IA/g at 48 h, giving a tumour-to-blood ratio of 1.6, which increases to 2.4 at 1 week post-injection.

titre: (11)C-acetate PET/CT in pre-therapeutic lymph node staging in high-risk prostate cancer patients and its influence on disease management - a retrospective study.
resume_court: The aims of this study were to evaluate the association between positive (11)C-acetate PET/CT findings and the estimated risk of pelvic lymph node metastases and to assess the impact of (11)C-acetate PET/CT on patient management in high-risk prostate cancer patients. The imaging results with (11)C-acetate PET/CT have a considerable impact on patient management.

titre: Synthesis and preclinical evaluation of DOTAGA-conjugated PSMA ligands for functional imaging and endoradiotherapy of prostate cancer.
resume_court: Due to its high expression in prostate cancer, PSMA (prostate-specific membrane antigen) represents an ideal target for both diagnostic imaging and endoradiotherapeutic approaches. The pair of diagnostic/therapeutic PSMA-ligands [(68)Ga/(177)Lu]DOTAGA-ffk(Sub-KuE) possess remarkable potential for the management of prostate cancer.

titre: Prospective randomized trial comparing magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)-guided in-bore biopsy to MRI-ultrasound fusion and transrectal ultrasound-guided prostate biopsy in patients with prior negative biopsies.
resume_court: A significant proportion of prostate cancers (PCas) are missed by conventional transrectal ultrasound-guided biopsy (TRUS-GB). It remains unclear whether the combined approach using targeted magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)-ultrasound fusion-guided biopsy (FUS-GB) and systematic TRUS-GB is superior to targeted MRI-guided in-bore biopsy (IB-GB) for PCa detection.

titre: Chemopreventive Effects of Korean Angelica versus Its Major Pyranocoumarins on Two Lineages of Transgenic Adenocarcinoma of Mouse Prostate Carcinogenesis.
resume_court: The growth of TRAMP dorsolateral prostate (DLP) in AGN- and D/DA-treated mice was inhibited by 66% and 61% at 16 weeks and by 67% and 72% at 28 weeks, respectively. Survival of mice bearing NE-Ca to 28 weeks was improved by AGN, but not by D/DA. Nevertheless, AGN- and D/DA-treated mice had lower NE-Ca burden.

titre: Initial Experience of (68)Ga-PSMA PET/CT Imaging in High-risk Prostate Cancer Patients Prior to Radical Prostatectomy.
resume_court: Median size of (68)Ga-PSMA-PET/CT-detected versus undetected LNMs was 13.6 versus 4.3mm (p<0.05). Conversely, (68)Ga-PSMA PET/CT enabled tumor visualization in the prostate. Overall, (68)Ga-PSMA PET/CT is a promising tool for functional imaging; however, our initial experience revealed substantial influence of LNM size on the diagnostic accuracy of (68)Ga-PSMA PET/CT.
