titre: A giant cavernous hemangioma of the liver extending into the pelvis.
resume_court: Giant cavernous hemangiomas are the most common tumors of the liver, ocurring in up to 20% of the general population. Although liver hemangiomas are extremely common, surgical treatment is rarely required. With appropriate indications, and when enucleation is not feasible or ideal, major liver resection is a safe alternative approach with excellent outcomes when performed in the right setting.

titre: Urologic cancers in Korea.
resume_court: The incidence and prevalence of prostate and kidney cancers have been increasing in Korea during the last decade, and a marked improvement in survival rates has been noted. A national comprehensive cancer database is needed for better insight into risk factors, selection of sequential strategies, tumor biology and survival outcome of Korean urologic cancer patients.

titre: Serial blood-based analysis of AR-V7 in men with advanced prostate cancer.
resume_court: Metastatic prostate cancer patients treated at Johns Hopkins with AR-directed therapies or taxane chemotherapies underwent serial liquid biopsies for CTC-based AR-V7 analysis at baseline, during therapy, and at progression. Patients selected for inclusion in this report were those who provided =4 CTC samples, at least one of which was AR-V7 positive, over the course of =2 consecutive therapies.

titre: Ten significantly differentially expressed genes in prostate cancer: Screening and verification
resume_court: To screen and verify differentially expressed genes in prostate cancer. A total of 1 444 genes were found to be differentially expressed (differentiation = 1.5-fold; P= 0.05) in the prostate cancer tissue, of which 769 (53%) were up-regulated and 675 (47%) down-regulated. Totally, 10 significantly differentially expressed genes were identified.

titre: Correlation of FOXA1 with the malignancy and progression of prostate cancer
resume_court: To study the relationship of the expression of FOXA1 in the prostate cancer (PCa) tissue with the Gleason score and clinical staging of PCa and with castration-resistant PCa (CRPC). Then we analyzed their correlation with the Gleason score and TNM staging of PCa and that with CRPC. The positive expression of FOXA1 is increased in PCa, most significantly in the advanced stage of the tumor.

titre: MicroRNAs and prostate cancer
resume_court: Prostate cancer (PCa) is one of the most common malignancies in the urinary system of males. This article focuses on the roles of microRNAs in the occurrence and progression of PCa, with a description of differentially expressed microRNAs in PCa and an analysis of their association with its prognosis as well as their correlation with chemotherapy, androgen receptors, and metastasis of PCa.

titre: Penile rehabilitation after radical pelvic surgery
resume_court: Prostate cancer, bladder cancer, and rectal cancer are common malignancies in the male pelvis. Early penile rehabilitation after surgery can improve or restore the erectile function of the patients. This article focuses on penile rehabilitation after radical pelvic surgery.

titre: Present condition and new vista of the future in robotic-assisted laparoscopic surgeries
resume_court: The introduction of robotic surgical system is one of the most exciting topic in the field of the surgery. We wish that this symposium would help the audience to understand the present condition and new vista of the future in robotic-assisted laparoscopic surgeries.

titre: A Family of Potent Ru(II) Photosensitizers with Enhanced DNA Intercalation: Bimodal Photokillers.
resume_court: A new family of Ru(II)-based photosensitizers was synthesized and systematically characterized. The complexes obtained carry either PF6- or Cl(-) counterions. The highest light-induced toxicity was conferred by the photosensitizers bearing Cl(-) counterions, probably due to the looser ionic "chaperoning" of Cl(-) , in comparison to PF6-, leading to higher cell internalization.

titre: Association between number of prostate biopsies and patient-reported functional outcomes after radical prostatectomy: implications for active surveillance protocols.
resume_court: To evaluate whether the number of preoperative prostate biopsies affects functional outcomes after radical prostatectomy (RP). Primary outcomes were urinary and erectile function at 12 months postoperatively. We did not find evidence that a greater number of preoperative prostate biopsies adversely affected erectile or urinary function at 12 months after RP.

titre: Insufficient Sleep and Risk of Prostate Cancer in a Large Swedish Cohort.
resume_court: There are some data to suggest that insufficient sleep, including short sleep duration and sleep disruption, may be associated with an increased risk of cancer. Habitual sleep duration and sleep disruption were self-reported in 1997. In this large prospective study from Sweden, we found no association between habitual sleep duration or sleep disruption and risk of prostate cancer.

titre: Methodology of patient care for elevated PSA after prostate cancer treatment: A primary care perspective.
resume_court: Prostate cancer (PCa) remains one of the most common cancers in men. About 15-18% of men treated for PCa will have an elevation of their PSA, which is a source of great concern and will lead to a management discussion with the patient. Approximately 25-33% of men with PCa will experience a recurrence of their cancer after surgery or radiation.

titre: A simple analytical method for heterogeneity corrections in low dose rate prostate brachytherapy.
resume_court: In low energy brachytherapy, the presence of tissue heterogeneities contributes significantly to the discrepancies observed between treatment plan and delivered dose. In this work, we present a simplified analytical dose calculation algorithm for heterogeneous tissue. Moreover, the algorithm is applicable for any type of heterogeneities.

titre: Bone Metastasis-Related MicroRNAs: New Targets for Treatment?
resume_court: MicroRNAs (miRNAs) are a new class of small noncoding RNAs of 19-25 nucleotides that function as negative posttranscriptional gene regulators. Finally, we discuss the exciting potential of using miRNAs as diagnostics and therapeutic targets to reduce the risk of bone metastases in cancer, from the perspective of data provided by recent pre-clinical and clinical studies.

titre: Association Between Older Age and Increasing Gleason Score.
resume_court: In order to help inform the discussion about the risks versus benefits of prostate cancer screening among older men, we determined whether advanced age is associated with a higher probability of harboring high-grade or high-risk disease. In addition, older men experienced a significant increase in the relative probability of high-risk or high-grade disease from 2007-2008 to 2010-2011.

titre: Body diffusion kurtosis imaging: Basic principles, applications, and considerations for clinical practice.
resume_court: Technologic advances enable performance of diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI) at ultrahigh b-values, where standard monoexponential model analysis may not apply. The novel technique, diffusion kurtosis imaging (DKI), enables characterization of non-Gaussian water diffusion behavior. Although still largely in the research phase, DKI is being explored in wider clinical settings.

titre: Long-term cancer control outcomes in patients with clinically high-risk prostate cancer treated with robot-assisted radical prostatectomy: results from a multi-institutional study of 1100 patients.
resume_court: Long-term cancer control outcomes in clinically high-risk prostate cancer (PCa) patients treated with robot-assisted radical prostatectomy (RARP) remain unknown. Outcomes consisted of BCR-free survival, CR-free survival, and salvage therapy rates. At 10 yr, BCR-free survival, CR-free survival, and salvage therapy rates were 50%, 87%, and 37%, respectively.

titre: Age is Associated with Upgrading at Confirmatory Biopsy among Men with Prostate Cancer Treated with Active Surveillance.
resume_court: Active surveillance is increasingly recommended for older men with low risk prostate cancer. We hypothesized that older age is associated with an increased risk of Gleason score upgrading at confirmatory biopsy when controlling for prostate volume. Older men who are interested in active surveillance should be counseled about the risks and benefits of confirmatory biopsy.

titre: Clonal Dynamics Reveal Two Distinct Populations of Basal Cells in Slow-Turnover Airway Epithelium.
resume_court: Epithelial lineages have been studied at cellular resolution in multiple organs that turn over rapidly. This pseudostratified epithelium contains basal cells and secretory and multiciliated luminal cells. We have thus revealed early luminal commitment of cells that are morphologically indistinguishable from stem cells.

titre: Targeting bone metastases in prostate cancer: improving clinical outcome.
resume_court: Bone metastases develop in most patients with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC). Understanding the pathophysiology of bone metastases resulted in the development of agents that improve clinical outcome, suggesting that managing both the systemic disease and associated bone events is important. Novel agents targeting tumour and bone cells are under clinical development.

titre: p63 controls cell migration and invasion by transcriptional regulation of MTSS1.
resume_court: Metastasis is a multistep cell-biological process, which is orchestrated by many factors, including metastasis activators and suppressors. However, recent findings indicate that MTSS1 acts as oncogene and pro-migratory factor in melanoma tumors. We reported that ?Np63 is able to drive the migration of breast tumor cells by inducing the expression of MTSS1.

titre: Heat-shock factor 2 is a suppressor of prostate cancer invasion.
resume_court: Heat-shock factors (HSFs) are key transcriptional regulators in cell survival. Here, we report that HSF2 suppresses tumor invasion of prostate cancer (PrCa). This study provides the first evidence for HSF2 acting as a suppressor of invasion in human malignancies.

titre: Factors associated with prostate cancer screening behavior among men over 50 in Fasa, Iran, based on the PRECEDE model.
resume_court: Prostate cancer is one of the most common and lethal cancers in the world. The purpose of this study was to investigate factors associated with prostate cancer screening behaviors among men over 50 in Fasa, Iran, based on the PRECEDE model. The prostate cancer screening behaviors in men over 50 in Fasa, Iran, were at a low level.

titre: Analysis of Prostate Deformation during a Course of Radiation Therapy for Prostate Cancer.
resume_court: Accurate analysis of the correlation between deformation of the prostate and displacement of its center of gravity (CoG) is important for efficient radiation therapy for prostate cancer. A single observer contoured the prostate gland only. The correlation between the displacement of the CoG and the local deformation of the prostate was evaluated using multiple regression analysis.

titre: Redox-Sensitive PEG-Polypeptide Nanoporous Particles for Survivin Silencing in Prostate Cancer Cells.
resume_court: We report the engineering of intracellular redox-responsive nanoporous poly(ethylene glycol)-poly(l-lysine) particles (NPEG-PLLs). A significant impairment of cell survival was observed in cells concomitantly exposed to paclitaxel and siRNA-loaded NPEG-PLLs. Overall, our findings indicate that NPEG-PLLs represent a highly loaded depot for the delivery of therapeutic nucleic acids to cancer cells.

titre: Tissue-specificity of heparan sulfate biosynthetic machinery in cancer.
resume_court: Heparan sulfate (HS) proteoglycans are key components of cell microenvironment and fine structure of their polysaccharide HS chains plays an important role in cell-cell interactions, adhesion, migration and signaling. However, cancer epithelial cells demonstrated common tendency to acquire fibroblast-like elongation-oriented mode of HS biosynthetic system.

titre: Novel Imidazopyridine Derivatives Possess Anti-Tumor Effect on Human Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer Cells.
resume_court: Prostate cancer (PCa) is the second leading cause of cancer-related death afflicting United States males. Thus, our results indicate the novel compound M-MeI to be a promising candidate for castration-resistant PCa therapy, and future studies investigating the mechanism of imidazopyridine inhibition may aid to the development of effective anti-PCa agents.

titre: Ablation of B7-H3 but Not B7-H4 Results in Highly Increased Tumor Burden in a Murine Model of Spontaneous Prostate Cancer.
resume_court: The costimulatory molecules B7-H3 and B7-H4 are overexpressed in a variety of human tumors and have been hypothesized as possible biomarkers and immunotherapeutic targets. By means of a highly physiologic, spontaneous tumor model in mice, we establish a causal link between B7-H3 and host tumor control and found B7-H4 to be redundant.
