resume_court: IGFBP-1 and IGFBP-2 are suppressed by growth hormone and therefore represent less prominent members of the IGFBP family when compared to IGFBP-3 that carries most of the IGFs during circulation under normal conditions in humans in vivo. Secretion of IGFBP-1 and IGFBP-2 is further suppressed by insulin and diminished with increasing obesity.

titre: The biomarker sex hormone-binding globulin - from established applications to emerging trends in clinical medicine.
resume_court: Sex hormone-binding globulin (SHBG) is a serum glycoprotein exhibiting the unique feature of binding sex steroids with high affinity and specificity. This review article portrays the different disorders associated with altered SHBG levels and discusses the usefulness of SHBG as disease biomarker from a clinicians as well as from an endocrinological researchers point of view.

titre: Arterial input functions (AIFs) measured directly from arteries with low and standard doses of contrast agent, and AIFs derived from reference tissues.
resume_court: Measurements of arterial input function (AIF) can have large systematic errors at standard contrast agent doses in dynamic contrast enhanced MRI (DCE-MRI). We compared measured AIFs from low dose (AIFLD) and standard dose (AIFSD) contrast agent injections, as well as the AIF derived from a muscle reference tissue and artery (AIFref). EMMs accurately fitted the AIFs.

titre: Peptide vaccines in breast cancer: The immunological basis for clinical response.
resume_court: This review discusses peptide-based vaccines in breast cancer, immune responses and clinical outcomes, which include studies on animal models and phase I, phase I/II, phase II and phase III clinical trials. Peptide-based vaccines are powerful neoadjuvant immunotherapies that can directly target proteins expressed in tumor cells, mainly tumor-associated antigens (TAAs).

titre: Trends in major cancer mortality in Korea, 1983-2012, with a joinpoint analysis.
resume_court: Cancer is the leading cause of death in Korea. ASRs for esophagus and liver cancers increased until the early 1990s and thereafter declined, leading to significant decreases [p<0.05] for esophagus cancer (APC: -1.85% for men and -3.82% for women) and liver cancer (APC: -1.55% for men and -0.56% for women) in 1983-2012. ASRs for uterine cancer peaked in 2003 and then declined (APC: 2.85%).

titre: Utilizing time-driven activity-based costing to understand the short- and long-term costs of treating localized, low-risk prostate cancer.
resume_court: Given the costs of delivering care for men with prostate cancer remain poorly described, this article reports the results of time-driven activity-based costing (TDABC) for competing treatments of low-risk prostate cancer. Substantial cost variation was observed at 5 years, with costs ranging from $7,298 for AS to $23,565 for IMRT, and they remained consistent through 12 years of follow-up.

titre: Improving the arterial input function in dynamic contrast enhanced MRI by fitting the signal in the complex plane.
resume_court: Dynamic contrast enhanced (DCE) imaging is a widely used technique in oncologic imaging. An essential prerequisite for obtaining quantitative values from DCE-MRI is the determination of the arterial input function (AIF). Furthermore, the dynamic behavior closely followed the AIF obtained with DCE-CT in the same patients (mean correlation coefficient: 0.92).

titre: Prognostic marker and target in prostate cancer.

Novel roles of androgen receptor, epidermal growth factor receptor, TP53, regulatory RNAs, NF-kappa-B, chromosomal translocations, neutrophil associated gelatinase, and matrix metalloproteinase-9 in prostate cancer and prostate cancer stem cells.
resume_court: Approximately one in six men will be diagnosed with some form of prostate cancer in their lifetime. Over 250,000 men worldwide die annually due to complications from prostate cancer. While advancements in prostate cancer screening and therapies have helped in lowering this statistic, better tests and more effective therapies are still needed.

titre: Is supplemental external beam radiation therapy essential to maximize brachytherapy outcomes in patients with unfavorable intermediate-risk disease?
resume_court: To evaluate whether supplemental external beam radiotherapy (EBRT) is essential to maximize Pd-103 brachytherapy outcomes in patients with unfavorable intermediate-risk (IR) disease. Median follow-up was 7.5 years. Although unfavorable IR patients had a greater incidence of BF, PCSM, and OM when compared with favorable IR, neither the addition nor dose of supplemental EBRT influenced outcome.

titre: The Effects of Focal Therapy for Prostate Cancer on Sexual Function: A Combined Analysis of Three Prospective Trials.
resume_court: Tissue preservation by means of focal therapy offers some men with clinically significant prostate cancer an alternative to standard care that appears to confer favourable genito-urinary outcomes. Median IIEF-erectile score at baseline was 23 (IQR 11-28). The only baseline determinants of postoperative erectile function were total IIEF and IIEF-erectile function scores (p=0.002).

titre: Size-adjusted Quantitative Gleason Score as a Predictor of Biochemical Recurrence after Radical Prostatectomy.
resume_court: The risk of biochemical recurrence (BCR) following radical prostatectomy for pathologic Gleason 7 prostate cancer varies according to the proportion of Gleason 4 component. All pathologic Gleason 7 cases were identified and assessed for quantity of Gleason pattern 4. Quantitative measures of Gleason pattern 4 predict BCR better than the traditional Gleason score.

titre: Trends in PET Scan Usage for Imaging of Patients Diagnosed With Nonmetastatic Urologic Cancer.
resume_court: The precise utility of positron emission tomography (PET) scanning for urologic cancers is not well defined. PET scans had been performed for 3.60% of patients with bladder cancer, 1.09% of those with prostate cancer, and 5.32% of those with RCC. The usage of PET scanning for bladder cancer, prostate cancer, and RCC is increasing but still very selective.

titre: Diagnosis of pelvic lymph node metastasis in prostate cancer using single optical fiber probe.
resume_court: Elastic light single-scattering spectroscopy system (ELSSS) is a biomedical tool which is used for detection of cancerous tissues ex-vivo. The ELSSS spectral data were compared against the "gold standard" histopathology results. In this study, it was shown that ELSSS system can accurately distinguish reactive and metastatic pelvic lymph nodes of prostate cancer with high PPV and NPV.

titre: Complex relationship between sex hormones, insulin resistance and leptin in men with and without prostatic disease.
resume_court: To assess sex hormones, leptin and insulin-resistance in men with prostate cancer (PCa) and benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH) and to study associations between androgens and histologic score of prostate tissue in PCa. After dividing men considering the presence of MS, leptin was higher and total testosterone was lower in MS patients in all the groups.

titre: Stage at presentation and survival outcomes of patients with Gleason 8-10 prostate cancer and low prostate-specific antigen.
resume_court: To evaluate outcomes for men with high Gleason score and low prostate-specific antigen (PSA) prostate cancer. A total of 37,283 patients were included. Patients with Gleason 8-10 cancer and PSA levels of<4.0ng/ml have more aggressive disease than those with PSA levels of 4 to 9.9ng/ml; these low PSA cancers behave more like those with PSA levels of 10 to 19.9ng/ml.

titre: Synthesis and biological evaluation of esters of 16-formyl-17-methoxy-dehydroepiandrosterone derivatives as inhibitors of 5a-reductase type 2.
resume_court: In this study, we investigated the in vitro effect of 16-formyl-17-methoxy dehydroepiandrosterone derivatives on the activity of 5a-reductase type 2 (5a-R2) obtained from human prostate. In this case, the augmentation of the lipophilicity of these dehydroepiandrosterone derivatives increased their potency as inhibitors of 5a-R2.

titre: Prostate cancer on computed tomography: A direct comparison with multi-parametric magnetic resonance imaging and tissue pathology.
resume_court: Multi-parametric prostate magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is considered the current imaging standard for detection and staging of prostate cancer. CT results were directly compared to multi-parametric MRI findings and biopsy results. The overall agreement of MRI and CT is 85.19% (95% CI: 67.52-94.08%).

titre: Diagnosis of prostate cancer via nanotechnological approach.
resume_court: Prostate cancer is one of the leading causes of cancer-related deaths among the Caucasian adult males in Europe and the USA. This review discusses the state-of-the-art research in the development of novel noninvasive prostate cancer diagnostics using nanotechnology coupled with suggested diagnostic strategies for their clinical implication.

titre: Calvarium and dura mater as delayed sites of distant metastasis from papillary thyroid carcinoma.
resume_court: Skull calvarium and dura mater are rare sites of distant metastasis, and mostly have been reported in lung, breast, and prostate malignancies. However, the calvarial and dural metastases from papillary thyroid cancer (PTC) are rare entities and pose diagnostic and therapeutic challenges. Calvarial and dural metastases from PTC are extremely rare clinical entities.

titre: Defining order and timing of mutations during cancer progression: the TO-DAG probabilistic graphical model.
resume_court: Somatic mutations arise and accumulate both during tumor genesis and progression. Such graphs represent the path and the waiting times of alterations during tumor evolution. TO-DAG shows high performance scores on synthetic data and recognizes mutations in gatekeeper tumor suppressor genes as trigger for several downstream mutational events in the human tumor data.

titre: A pilot study of the association of manganese superoxide dismutase and glutathione peroxidase 1 single gene polymorphisms with prostate cancer and serum prostate specific antigen levels.
resume_court: The aim of the study was to evaluate the potential association of single gene polymorphisms of the antioxidant enzymes manganese superoxide dismutase (MnSOD) and glutathione peroxidase (GPX1) with prostate cancer (PCa). Furthermore, an overall protective effect of the Ala allele of the MnSOD polymorphism on PCa risk was detected.

titre: Integrating Geriatric Assessment into Decision-Making after Prostatectomy: Adjuvant Radiotherapy, Salvage Radiotherapy, or None?
resume_court: Despite current advancements in the field, management of older prostate cancer patients still remains a big challenge for Geriatric Oncology. This article outlines the principles that should be observed in the management of elderly patients who have recently undergone prostatectomy for malignancy or with a biochemical relapse following prostatectomy.

titre: ILs-3, 6 and 11 increase, but ILs-10 and 24 decrease stemness of human prostate cancer cells in vitro.
resume_court: Cancer stem cells (CSCs) are associated with cancer recurrence and metastasis. In conclusion, our results suggest that ILs-3, 6 and 11 function as tumor promoters while ILs-10 and 24 function as tumor suppressors in the prostate cancer cell lines PC-3 and LNCaP in vitro, and such differences may attribute to their different effect on the stemness of PCa cells.

titre: The Diagnostic Performance of Multiparametric Magnetic Resonance Imaging to Detect Significant Prostate Cancer.
resume_court: We assess the accuracy of multiparametric magnetic resonance imaging for significant prostate cancer detection before diagnostic biopsy in men with an abnormal prostate specific antigen/digital rectal examination. PI-RADS 3 to 5 was considered positive. Multiparametric magnetic resonance imaging was positive in 77.0% of patients, 62.5% had prostate cancer and 41.6% had significant prostate cancer.

titre: Use of Biomarkers in Screening for Cancer.
resume_court: Screening for premalignant lesions or early invasive disease has the potential to reduce mortality from cancer. Although biomarkers have many attractive features as cancer screening tests, lack of sensitivity and specificity, when combined with the low prevalence of specific cancer types in asymptomatic subjects, limit their application for the early detection of malignancy.

titre: The Role of Epigenomics in the Study of Cancer Biomarkers and in the Development of Diagnostic Tools.
resume_court: Epigenetics plays a key role in cancer development. Epigenetics provides a mechanism to explain the development of cancer in such situations. This chapter describes epigenetic biomarkers as they are expressed during cancer development and their potential use in cancer diagnosis and prognosis.

titre: Prostate Specific Antigen as a Tumor Marker in Prostate Cancer: Biochemical and Clinical Aspects.
resume_court: In this chapter the use of prostate specific antigen (PSA) as a tumor marker for prostate cancer is discussed. Many PSA-based markers have been developed to improve the performance characteristics of tPSA. The prostate health index (phi), PSA-density (PSAD) and the contribution of non PSA-based markers such as the urinary transcripts of PCA3 and TMPRSS-ERG fusion are also discussed.

titre: Components of the Plasminogen-Plasmin System as Biologic Markers for Cancer.
resume_court: Members of the plasminogen-plasmin (PP) system participate in many physiologic functions. Thus, quantification of uPA, uPAR and PAI-1 in tumors and, in some cases in the circulating blood, became of potential value in the prognostication of many types of cancer. Hopefully the use of these biomarkers will be applied to other types of cancer in the near future.

titre: Urinary Prostate Cancer Antigen 3 as a Tumour Marker: Biochemical and Clinical Aspects.
resume_court: Due to low specificity of Prostate-Specific Antigen (PSA) we face a certain risk of overdiagnosis and overtreatment of Prostate Cancer (PCa). The benefits and harms of PSA-screening are controversially discussed. To overcome this weakness of PSA novel PCa biomarkers and detection tools are required.The urine-based biomarker Prostate Cancer Antigen 3 (PCA3) has been shown to be highly PCa-specific.

titre: The Role of CTCs as Tumor Biomarkers.
resume_court: Detection of Circulating Tumor Cells (CTCs) in peripheral blood can serve as a "liquid biopsy" approach and as a source of valuable tumor markers. CTCs are rare, and thus their detection, enumeration and molecular characterization are very challenging.

titre: Does previous transurethral prostate surgery affect oncologic and continence outcomes after RARP?
resume_court: We examined the effect of previous transurethral resection of the prostate (TURP) on multiple oncologic and continence outcomes after robotic-assisted radical prostatectomy (RARP). Patients were stratified into 49 patients who had previous TURP prior to RARP (group 1) and 2644 patients who had no TURP prior to RARP (group 2). This data can be used to counsel those with prior TURP before RARP.

titre: 3-Bromopyruvate induces rapid human prostate cancer cell death by affecting cell energy metabolism, GSH pool and the glyoxalase system.
resume_court: 3-bromopyruvate (3-BP) is an anti-tumour drug effective on hepatocellular carcinoma and other tumour cell types, which affects both glycolytic and mitochondrial targets, depleting cellular ATP pool. The drastic reduction of cellular ATP levels and depletion of GSH pool, associated with significant increase in cell oxidative stress, were found after 3-BP treatment of PC-3 cells.

titre: Focal cryoablation for unilateral low-intermediate-risk prostate cancer: 63-month mean follow-up results of 41 patients.
resume_court: To report (1) intermediate-term oncologic and functional outcomes of primary focal cryoablation (FC) in selected patients with clinically unilateral, low-intermediate-risk prostate cancer, and investigate (2) the impact of patient selection criteria at predicting outcomes after FC. The 2007 Task Force criteria appear to reduce the positive biopsy rate in contralateral lobe after FC.

titre: Independent predictors of prolonged operative time during robotic-assisted radical prostatectomy.
resume_court: The objective of this study is to investigate the determinants of prolonged operative time during robotic radical prostatectomy (RARP) after the learning curve period. The mean complete operative time was 187 � 32 min. Multivariable logistic regression revealed four independent predictors of prolonged operative time: blood loss, pre-operative PSA, robot malfunction, and gland volume.

titre: Oncological outcomes following robotic-assisted radical prostatectomy in a multiracial Asian population.
resume_court: This study evaluates the oncological outcomes of RARP in a multiracial Asian population from a single institution. The pathological stage was pT2 in 68.6% (n = 497/725), pT3 in 31.3% (n = 227/725) and n = 1 patient with pT4 disease. The pathological Gleason scores (GS) were 6 in 27.9% (n = 202/725), GS 7 in 63.6% (n = 461/725) and GS = 8 in 8.0 % (n = 58/725).

titre: Side docking of the da Vinci robotic system for radical prostatectomy: advantages over traditional docking.
resume_court: A cohort of 120 patients submitted to RARP were prospectively randomized into two groups by docking approach: SD with the patient supine with lower limbs slightly abducted on the operating table, and TD docking time, intraoperative number of collisions between the robotic arms and postoperative neurological problems in the lower limbs were noted. The SD approach is technically feasible.

titre: Robotic-assisted radical prostatectomy is less stressful than the open approach: results of a contemporary prospective study evaluating pathophysiology of cortisol stress-related kinetics in prostate cancer surgery.
resume_court: The objective of this study was to investigate the effects of prostate cancer (PCA) surgery on the stress system and to identify potential independent factors associating with stress recovery. The effects of PCA surgery on the stress system were measured by cortisol serum levels before and after surgery on post-operative day (POD) 0, 1, 3, 5 and 45. RARP was performed in 71% of cases.

titre: Octreotide in combination with AT-101 induces cytotoxicity and apoptosis through up-regulation of somatostatin receptors 2 and 5 in DU-145 prostate cancer cells.
resume_court: Prostate cancer (PCa) is the most common type of cancer among males. Octreotide in combination with AT-101 inhibited cell viability and induced apoptosis synergistically in DU-145 cells as compared to any agent alone. Combination treatment increased both SSTR2 and SSTR5 mRNA and protein levels in DU-145 cells.

titre: Patterns of HIV viremia and viral suppression before diagnosis of non-AIDS-defining cancers in HIV-infected individuals.
resume_court: The association between HIV viremia and non-AIDS-defining cancers (NADCs) is not well characterized. In the year before cancer diagnosis, 66 % of all patients were virally suppressed. Patients with anal cancer and Hodgkin lymphoma had the highest proportion of high level viremia in the ten years before cancer and the lowest frequency of viral load suppression at cancer diagnosis.

titre: Proteomic Profiling of Serum-Derived Exosomes from Ethnically Diverse Prostate Cancer Patients.
resume_court: Prostate cancer (PCa) remains the most frequently diagnosed male malignancy in Western countries and the second most common cause of male cancer death in the United States. This study demonstrates that small membrane-bound vesicles shed from the tumor called exosomes contain ethnically and tumor-specific biomarkers, and could be exploited for their diagnostic and therapeutic potential.

titre: Phosphorylation of nucleophosmin at threonine 234/237 is associated with HCC metastasis.
resume_court: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is frequently complicated by the occurrence of intrahepatic and extrahepatic metastases, leading to poor prognosis. To improve the prognosis for HCC patients, there is an urgent need to understand the molecular mechanisms of metastasis in HCC. Identification of CDK1/p-NPM/ROCK2 signaling pathway provides a novel target for molecular therapy against HCC metastasis.

titre: Metformin and prostate cancer mortality: a meta-analysis.
resume_court: Observational studies report conflicting results on the association between metformin exposure and prostate cancer outcomes. Metformin use was associated with improved overall survival in studies with clear risk window definition (HR 0.88, 95 % CI 0.86-0.90, p < 0.001) and in studies with potential immortal time bias (HR 0.52, 95 % CI 0.41-0.65, p < 0.001).

titre: Group sequential testing of the predictive accuracy of a continuous biomarker with unknown prevalence.
resume_court: Group sequential testing procedures have been proposed as an approach to conserving resources in biomarker validation studies. First, we develop asymptotic theory for the sequential empirical PPV and NPV curves when the prevalence must be estimated, rather than assumed known in a case-control study. Copyright � 2015 John Wiley & Sons, Ltd.

titre: Younger British men's understandings of prostate cancer: A qualitative study.
resume_court: The purpose of this study was to explore young British men's understandings of prostate health and cancer of the prostate. Accounts are discussed with reference to implications for improving men's understandings of prostate cancer, and likelihood of self-referral for prostate screening where necessary.

titre: Impact of Prostate Cancer Treatment on the Sexual Quality of Life for Men-Who-Have-Sex-with-Men.
resume_court: With earlier prostate cancer (PCa) diagnosis and an increased focus on survivorship, post-treatment sexual quality of life (QoL) has become increasingly important. We aimed to create a validated instrument for assessing sexual needs and concerns of MSM post-PCa treatment. Here we explore post-PCa treatment sexual concerns for a sample of MSM, as the first part of this multi-phase project.

titre: Clinical Relevance of Androgen Receptor Splice Variants in Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer.
resume_court: Metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC) currently benefits from a wealth of treatment options, yet still remains lethal in the vast majority of patients. AR-V7 appears to be the most relevant AR splice variant, and early clinical data suggest that it is a negative prognostic marker in mCRPC.

titre: Oral antibiotics in trans-rectal prostate biopsy and its efficacy to reduce infectious complications: Systematic review.
resume_court: For the diagnosis of prostate cancer trans-rectal prostate biopsy (TRPB) is used commonly, the procedure is associated with infective complications. To systematically review different regimens of prophylactic oral ABx in TRPB. Unexpectedly, ABx-resistant bacteria were identified more often in the single dose cohorts.

titre: Is Radical Perineal Prostatectomy a Viable Therapeutic Option for Intermediate- and High-risk Prostate Cancer?
resume_court: The proportion of HR PCa was 40.3%, 46.8%, and 49.5% in RPP, RRP, and MIRP (P < 0.001), respectively. Biochemical recurrence-free survival rates among RPP, RRP, and MIRP were 73.0%, 70.1%, and 76.8%, respectively, at 5 yr (RPP vs. RPP, P = 0.02; RPP vs. MIRP, P = 0.23). RPP achieved acceptable oncological control for IR and HR PCa.

titre: Extracting the Benefit of Nexrutine(�) for Cancer Prevention.
resume_court: The current standard of care for prostate cancer includes hormone therapy, radiation therapy and radical prostatectomy, each with its own set of undesirable side effects. In addition we have summarized the emerging evidence regarding the use of Nexrutine(�) in other tumor models to demonstrate the potential benefits of Nexrutine(�).

titre: Circulating levels of adipocytokine omentin-1 in patients with renal cell cancer.
resume_court: Renal cell carcinoma (RCC) is the fifth most common cancer worldwide, and becomes one of the leading causes of genitourinary cancer-related death in both males and females. The omentin-1 levels in healthy people were 9.86�1.44ng/mL and the circulating omentin-1 levels were dramatically decreased to 3.62�0.76ng/mL in RCC patients (p<0.001).

titre: Erectile function after radical prostatectomy: Do patients return to baseline?
resume_court: The aim of this study was to assess postprostatectomy erectile function compared to preoperative status by subjective patient perception and the abbreviated International Index of Erectile Function (IIEF-5) questionnaire. Secondary outcome measures included the proportion of patients returning to baseline erectile function according to the IIEF-5 and predictors of return to baseline function.

titre: Impact of magnetic resonance imaging-guided prostate biopsy in the supine position on the detection of significant prostate cancer in an inhomogeneous patient cohort.
resume_court: The aim of this study was to determine the tumour detection rate of magnetic resonance-guided biopsy (MRGB) in the supine position for significant prostate cancer in an inhomogeneous patient cohort. No significant differences were found between the numbers of tumour-positive and tumour-negative collected cores. The biopsy method could be a reasonable alternative to MRGB in the prone position.

titre: Expectant management of veterans with early-stage prostate cancer.
resume_court: For certain men with low-risk prostate cancer, aggressive treatment results in marginal survival benefits while exposing them to urinary and sexual side effects. Nevertheless, expectant management has been underused. In the current study, the authors evaluated the association between various factors and expectant management use among veterans diagnosed with prostate cancer.

titre: Screening key microRNAs for castration-resistant prostate cancer based on miRNA/mRNA functional synergistic network.
resume_court: High-throughput methods have been used to explore the mechanisms by which androgen-sensitive prostate cancer (ASPC) develops into castration-resistant prostate cancer (CRPC). In this study, we performed systematic and integrative analysis to detect key miRNAs that contribute to CRPC development. Two of the miRNAs (miR-125b and miR-124) have previously been shown to be related to CRPC.

titre: Social inequalities and cancer: can the European deprivation index predict patients' difficulties in health care access? a pilot study.
resume_court: The European Deprivation Index (EDI), is a new ecological estimate for Socio-Economic Status (SES). The association of EDI and Time-To-Diagnosis (TTD), as well as Time-To-Treatment (TTT) was analyzed using a cox regression, and a strata analysis per tumor site was performed. EDI quintiles were not found associated with either TTT or TTD.

titre: Image-guided intensity-modulated radiotherapy of prostate cancer: Analysis of interfractional errors and acute toxicity.
resume_court: The aim of the study was to estimate interfractional deviations in patient and prostate position, the impact of the frequency of online verification on the treatment margins, and to assess acute radiation reactions of high-dose external beam image-guided intensity-modulated radiotherapy (IG-IMRT) of localized prostate cancer. The median total dose was 79.2 Gy (range 77.4-81.0 Gy).

titre: Isolation and analysis of discreet human prostate cellular populations.
resume_court: The use of lineage tracing in transgenic mouse models has revealed an abundance of subcellular phenotypes responsible for maintaining prostate homeostasis. The ability to use fresh human tissues to examine the hypotheses generated by these mouse experiments has been greatly enhanced by technical advances in tissue processing, flow cytometry and cell culture.

titre: Sequential Registration-Based Segmentation of the Prostate Gland in MR Image Volumes.
resume_court: Accurate and fast segmentation and volume estimation of the prostate gland in magnetic resonance (MR) images are necessary steps in the diagnosis, treatment, and monitoring of prostate cancer. The proposed algorithm exploits the inter-slice similarity of volumetric MR image series to achieve highly accurate results while significantly reducing the contouring time.

titre: Suppression of BCL2 by Antisense Oligonucleotides and Compensation by Non-Targeted Genes May Enhance Tumor Proliferation.
resume_court: Antisense oligonucleotides have been used to target regulatory proteins in both in vivo and in vitro models of prostate cancer. The net result was an altered pattern of gene expression often associated with more aggressive and proliferative tumors. As a result, we propose that oligonucleotide-mediated treatment could be more effective when directed towards KI-67 and BCL2.

titre: Primary Care Attributes Associated with Receipt of Preventive Care Services: A National Study.
resume_court: Primary care attributes (PCAs) encompassed by patient-centered medical homes may increase receipt of preventive care, though national studies are lacking. The total PCA score was positively associated with increased receipt of each preventive care measure. Individual primary care attributes except enhanced access were positively associated with each preventive care measure.

titre: Sexual health and relationships after age 60.
resume_court: A commonly used phrase describing aging is "60 is the new 40". Biological aging challenges physical sexual activity and responsiveness. Regrettably, there is a very modest literature on sexual health and associated possible interventions in older patients in these cohorts.

titre: Subrenal capsule grafting technology in human cancer modeling and translational cancer research.
resume_court: Patient-derived xenograft (PDX) cancer models with high fidelity are in great demand. While the majority of PDXs are grafted under the skin of immunodeficient mice, the Living Tumor Laboratory (LTL), using unique subrenal capsule grafting techniques, has successfully established more than 200 transplantable PDX models of various low to high grade human cancers.

titre: Correlation between the germline methylation status in ERß promoter and the risk in prostate cancer: a prospective study.
resume_court: Familial aggregation of cancer may reflect an overall contribution of inherited genes or a shared mechanism for the manipulation of gene function. Expression of ERß was detected at both transcriptional and translational levels. Taken together, our results support the conclusion that abnormal methylation of the ERß promoter may increase genetic susceptibility to prostate cancer.

titre: Probiotics: a proactive approach to health. A symposium report.
resume_court: This report summarises talks given at the 8th International Yakult Symposium, held on 23-24 April 2015 in Berlin. Finally, an insight was given on a recent expert meeting, which re-examined the probiotic definition, advised on the appropriate use and scope of the term and outlined different probiotic categories and the prevalence of different mechanisms of activity.

titre: Perception and satisfaction with the information received during the medical care process in patients with prostate cancer.
resume_court: To assess the perception and degree of satisfaction of Spanish patients with prostate cancer (PC) concerning the information received during the medical care process. Some 90.2% of the patients stated that they had received, mainly from the urologist, an appropriate amount of information about the disease.

titre: Prognostic and predictive biomarkers in prostate cancer.
resume_court: Prostate cancer (PCa) is one of the leading causes of cancer death among males, especially in more developed countries. Early detection of PCa has led to a substantial decline in the number of metastatic patients. However, the prostate-specific antigen screening test has proved to be a double-edged sword so far, as it also accounts for PCa overdiagnosis.

titre: MALT lymphoma of the prostate: Place of radiotherapy. Case report and discussion
resume_court: We report the case of a patient presenting with MALT (mucosa-associated lymphoid tissue) lymphoma of the prostate, who received an irradiation delivering 30.6 Gy in 17 fractions after transurethral resection. With a follow-up of 6 years, he remained alive and free of disease. In view of the literature and this case report, definitive local irradiation should be administered in this rare disease.

titre: Predictors and rate of adjuvant radiation therapy following radical prostatectomy: A report from the Prostate Cancer Registry.
resume_court: Long-term data from three randomized trials have demonstrated that adjuvant radiation therapy (ART) reduces the rate of biochemical failure in high-risk men following radical prostatectomy (RP). Of these eligible prostatectomy cases, a total of 89 received ART. A subgroup of 833 men had an adverse pathologic feature, of whom 78 received ART.

titre: Cytotoxic compounds from Laurencia pacifica.
resume_court: The current investigation sought to explore the nature of the secondary metabolites in the algae, Laurencia pacifica. Isoaplysin (1) and debromoaplysinol (4) were up to fourfold more potent in cancer-derived cell populations than in non-tumor-derived normal cells (MCF10A). These analogues are promising candidates for anticancer drug development.

titre: 4-Hydroxybenzoic acid derivatives as HDAC6-specific inhibitors modulating microtubular structure and HSP90a chaperone activity against prostate cancer.
resume_court: Histone deacetylase (HDAC)6 is a unique isoenzyme targeting specific substrates including a-tubulin and heat shock protein (HSP)90. Both compounds strongly enhanced a-tubulin acetylation leading to remodeling of microtubular organization. Collectively, our data support the potential of 4-hydroxybenzoic acid derivatives as HDAC6-specific inhibitors with anti-cancer properties.

titre: A Delphi consensus study on salvage brachytherapy for prostate cancer relapse after radiotherapy, a Uro-GEC study.
resume_court: Patients treated with low radiotherapy dose or treated at young age are at a risk of developing local relapse. After the final round consensus was reached on 17 out of 38 (45%) questions. Consensus was reached in 52% of questions about patient selection, in 50% of the questions about diagnostic tests and in 22% of the questions on performing salvage prostate brachytherapy.

titre: SIMBOSPROST: Prevalence of metabolic syndrome and osteoporosis in prostate cancer patients treated with radiotherapy and androgen deprivation therapy: A multicentre, cross-sectional study.
resume_court: To assess the prevalence of metabolic syndrome (MetS) and osteoporosis in patients with prostate cancer (PCa) treated with radical radiotherapy (RT) with or without androgen deprivation therapy (ADT). MetS prevalence was 50% in the control group. The prevalence of MetS in pts with PCa treated with radical RT was higher (47%) than in the general population.

titre: Long non-coding RNA UCA1 contributes to the progression of prostate cancer and regulates proliferation through KLF4-KRT6/13 signaling pathway.
resume_court: Long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) UCA1 have been shown to paly an important regulatory roles in cancer biology, and UCA1 dysfunction is related to TNM stage, metastasis and postoperative survival in several cancers. Moreover, UCA1 loss-of-function inhibited cell proliferation and induced cell apoptosis, at least partially, through inactivation KLF4-KRT6/13 cascade.

titre: Metformin therapy and prostate cancer risk: a meta-analysis of observational studies.
resume_court: Several observational studies have shown that metformin therapy may modify the risk of prostate cancer. We searched pubmed database (January 1966-February 2014) for case-control and cohort studies that assessed metformin therapy and prostate cancer risk. Our findings indicate that metformin therapy is not significantly associated with lower prostate cancer risk.

titre: Perineural invasion is an independent predictor of biochemical recurrence of prostate cancer after local treatment: a meta-analysis.
resume_court: Controversy still existed regarding the role of perineural invasion (PNI) in prostate cancer. PNI predicted BCR of prostate cancer in both RP (HR 1.51, 95% CI 1.23-1.85) and biopsy specimens (HR 1.68, 95% CI 1.36-2.09). PNI was demonstrated to be associated with higher risk for BCR of prostate cancer after local treatment.

titre: Preoperative risk factors for early postoperative urinary continence recovery after non-nerve-sparing radical prostatectomy in Chinese patients: a single institute retrospective analysis.
resume_court: Urinary incontinence (UI) remained a significant complication after radical prostatectomy and led to impaired quality of life. The results suggested preoperative PFME was the only independent protective risk factor for immediate continence after catheter removal. Our results supported that age and preoperative PFME were predictive factors for early continence after RP.

titre: Quantitative differences in [(18)F] NaF PET/CT: TOF versus non-TOF measurements.
resume_court: [(18)F] sodium fluoride (NaF) PET/CT is a current, clinically relevant method to assess bone metastases. All osseous structures showed higher SUVmean for TOF compared to non-TOF including normal regions, degenerative joint disease, and metastases. The differences in TOF vs. non-TOF images should be considered when evaluating response to therapy and in the design of multi-center clinical trials.

titre: The use of dynamic nuclear polarization (13)C-pyruvate MRS in cancer.
resume_court: In recent years there has been an immense development of new targeted anti-cancer drugs. The use of DNP enhanced (13)C-pyruvate has in preclinical studies shown to be a sensitive method for detecting cancer and for assessment of early treatment response in a variety of cancers. However, more studies are needed in order to establish use of hyperpolarized (13)C MRS imaging of cancer.

titre: Epithelial-mesenchymal transition in prostatic disease.
resume_court: Considering the cellular heterogeneity that characterizes both conditions, identifying the transcriptional programming of the phenotypic framework defining EMT and its reverse process mesenchymal-epithelial transition in their pathological landscape will enable novel platforms for biomarker-driven therapeutics and their implementation in benign prostatic hyperplasia and prostate cancer.

titre: Kindlin-2 promotes invasiveness of prostate cancer cells via NF-?B-dependent upregulation of matrix metalloproteinases.
resume_court: Invasive progression is the major lethal cause of prostate cancer. Conversely, overexpression of kindlin-2 promoted the invasiveness of prostate cancer cells. Further studies are warranted to evaluate the significance of kindlin-2 as a therapeutic target for metastatic prostate cancer.

titre: New bigenic mouse model increases the understanding of genetic synergism in the progression of prostate cancer.
resume_court: A new bigenic mouse model, engineered with the overexpression of PSGR and the knockout of PTEN, has been used to study the relationship between 2 genes and disease progression. A study in Oncogene (Rodriguez et al.) has shown that these 2 genetic polymorphisms synergistically promote the development of prostate cancer.

titre: Nucleoporin 62 and Ca(2+)/calmodulin dependent kinase kinase 2 regulate androgen receptor activity in castrate resistant prostate cancer cells.
resume_court: Re-activation of the transcriptional activity of the androgen receptor (AR) is an important factor mediating progression from androgen-responsive to castrate-resistant prostate cancer (CRPC). The abundance of CaMKK2 in nuclear fractions of androgen-responsive prostate cancer and CRPC, cells were determined by subcellular fractionation and Western blotting.

titre: Germline copy number variation analysis in Finnish families with hereditary prostate cancer.
resume_court: The inherited factors that predispose individuals to prostate cancer (PrCa) remain largely unknown. The deletion associated with an increased PrCa risk (P?=?0.018, OR?=?2.06, 95%CI?=?1.18-3.61). A novel association between the EPHA3 deletion and PrCa risk was observed and, if confirmed, screening for this variant may aid in risk stratification among HPC patients.

titre: Primary mucinous adenocarcinoma of the female urethra: a contemporary clinicopathologic analysis.
resume_court: Primary mucinous adenocarcinoma of the female urethra is very rare and may lead to both diagnostic and therapeutic challenges. A search was made through the files of 2 major academic institutions for cases of confirmed primary mucinous adenocarcinoma arising from the female urethra. Immunohistochemical stains for GATA3, p63, CK7, CK20, CDX2, ER, PAX8, and ß-catenin were performed on all cases.

titre: Cancer and Its Association With the Development of Coronary Artery Calcification: An Assessment From the Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis.
resume_court: Increase in pre-existing CAC was compared in these groups using linear regression of log transformed CAC. In participants with CAC at baseline, a clear difference of CAC progression was not observed between cancer and noncancer participants (P=0.6 for women, P=0.2 for men). However, in individuals with pre-existing CAC, it is not clear whether the presence of cancer accelerates CAC over time.

titre: Defining the Incremental Utility of Prostate Multiparametric Magnetic Resonance Imaging at Standard and Specialized Read in Predicting Extracapsular Extension of Prostate Cancer.
resume_court: Multiparametric magnetic resonance imaging (mpMRI) is increasingly used in staging early prostate cancer (PCa) but remains heavily reader-dependent. We obtained radiologic prediction of pECE from standard radiologic reports (standard read) and by a specialized reader blinded to clinical and pathologic findings (specialized read).

titre: Suppressed glycolytic metabolism in the prostate of transgenic rats overexpressing calcium-binding protein regucalcin underpins reduced cell proliferation.
resume_court: Regucalcin (RGN) is a calcium-binding protein underexpressed in human prostate cancer cases, and it has been associated with the suppression of cell proliferation and the regulation of several metabolic pathways. The present findings also suggest that the loss of RGN may predispose to a hyper glycolytic profile and fostered proliferation of prostate cells.

titre: Expression of androgen receptor splice variants in clinical breast cancers.
resume_court: The importance of androgen receptor (AR) signaling is increasingly being recognized in breast cancer, which has elicited clinical trials aimed at assessing the efficacy of androgen deprivation therapy (ADT) for metastatic disease. These findings have implications for treatment response in the ongoing clinical trials of ADT in breast cancer.

titre: Genetic Evidence for XPC-KRAS Interactions During Lung Cancer Development.
resume_court: Lung cancer causes more deaths than breast, colorectal and prostate cancers combined. DNA repair deficiency is known to contribute to lung cancer development. Our results suggest that XPC may help repair DNA damage caused by KRAS-mediated production of ROS.

titre: Value of MRI/ultrasound fusion in primary biopsy for the diagnosis of prostate cancer
resume_court: Multiparametric magnetic resonance imaging (mpMRI) plays an emerging role in prostate cancer diagnosis. We compared the cancer detection rates of targeted biopsy (tB) of suspicious lesions in mpMRI versus systematic transperineal saturation biopsy (sB) in men with primary suspicion of prostate cancer (PCa). Of 80 high-grade PCa with GS =?4?+?3, 70 were diagnosed by sB, and 60 by tB (p?=?0.007).

titre: Broccoli-Derived Sulforaphane and Chemoprevention of Prostate Cancer: From Bench to Bedside.
resume_court: Sulforaphane (SFN) is a metabolic by product of cruciferous vegetables and is the biologically active phytochemical found in high concentrations in broccoli. The immediate precursor of SFN is glucoraphanin, a glucosinolate which requires metabolic conversion to SFN. The present review aims to focus specifically on SFN and its chemopreventive and antineoplastic activity against prostate cancer.

titre: Integrating Patient-Reported Outcome Measures into Routine Cancer Care: Cancer Patients' and Clinicians' Perceptions of Acceptability and Value.
resume_court: Despite growing interest in integrating patient-reported outcome (PRO) measures of symptoms and functional status into routine cancer care, little attention has been paid to patients' and clinicians' perceptions of acceptability and value. A two-phase qualitative study was conducted to develop a web-based PRO screening system with 21 items assessing symptoms (e.g., nausea) and functional status.

titre: Statins and cancers.
resume_court: Statins (inhibitors of 3-hydroxy-3-methyl-glutaryl-coenzyme A reductase) are a group of drugs used to treat lipid disorders. Numerous studies point to different possible effects of statins on cancer cells. Due to different pharmacokinetic properties of individual statins, they may have opposite effects on the risk of cancer.

titre: Anti-androgenic effects of flavonols in prostate cancer.
resume_court: Dietary-derived agents, such as the flavonoids, are of particular interest for prostate cancer (PCa) chemoprevention as they may offer a favourable safety and side-effect profile. An agent that demonstrates action on the androgen receptor (AR) axis may have value for preventing or treating castrate-resistant PCa.

titre: A comprehensive evaluation of machine learning techniques for cancer class prediction based on microarray data.
resume_court: Prostate cancer is among the most common cancer in males and its heterogeneity is well known. Various techniques were implied on prostate cancer data set in order to accurately predict cancer class including machine learning techniques. Further, a comprehensive evaluation of ten state-of-the-art machine learning techniques for their accuracy in class prediction of prostate cancer is done.

titre: Neoadjuvant Systemic Therapy Before Radical Prostatectomy in High-Risk Prostate Cancer Does Not Increase Surgical Morbidity: Contemporary Results Using the Clavien System.
resume_court: Multimodality therapies for men with high- and very high-risk prostate cancer, including neoadjuvant systemic therapy followed by subsequent radical prostatectomy (RP) are being increasingly explored despite the lack of adequate morbidity data. All complications within 90 days of surgery were defined and categorized by a 5-grade and 10-domain modification of the Clavien system.

titre: Validation of an Age-adjusted Prostate Cancer-Specific Comorbidity Index.
resume_court: Estimating competing mortality is of paramount importance for prostate cancer screening candidates and men with early prostate cancer. With stratification by the age-adjusted prostate cancer-specific comorbidity index, the 10-yr competing mortality rate in men selected for radical prostatectomy is approximately half as high as in unselected patients at the same level of comorbid risk.

titre: Diffusion-weighted MRI for early detection and characterization of prostate cancer in the transgenic adenocarcinoma of the mouse prostate model.
resume_court: To improve early diagnosis of prostate cancer to aid clinical decision-making. DW-MRI is a tool for early detection of cancer, and discrimination between cancer stages in the TRAMP model. The incorporation of DW-MRI-based prostate cancer stratification and monitoring could increase the accuracy of preclinical trials using TRAMP mice.

titre: Meeting the unmet support needs of BME men with prostate cancer.
resume_court: Men with prostate cancer from black and minority ethnic (BME) communities have reported many unmet information and support needs. A literature review identified the many challenges health professionals face in addressing these unmet needs, and suggested that not enough is known about the psychosocial effects of a prostate cancer diagnosis on men from BME communities in the UK.

titre: Fruit and vegetable intakes and risk of colorectal cancer and incident and recurrent adenomas in the PLCO cancer screening trial.
resume_court: The roles of fruits and vegetables in colorectal cancer development are unclear. Fruit and vegetable intake was measured using a self-reported dietary questionnaire. Our results suggest that increased fruit and vegetable intake may protect against multiple adenoma development and may reduce the detrimental effects of high processed meat intakes on colorectal cancer risk.

titre: Cancer Cell Radiobiological Studies Using In-House-Developed a-Particle Irradiator.
resume_court: An a-particle irradiator, enabling high-precision irradiation of cells for in vitro studies, has been constructed. Three prostate cancer (LNCaP, DU145, PC3) and three pancreatic cancer (Capan-1, Panc-1, BxPC-3) cell lines were irradiated by a-particles to the absorbed doses 0, 0.5, 1, and 2?Gy. For reference, cells were irradiated using (137)Cs to the absorbed doses 0, 1, 2, 4, 6, 8, and 10?Gy.

titre: Prospects for the future of prostate cancer vaccines.
resume_court: Cancer therapy is undergoing a revolution fueled by clinical data demonstrating that the immune system has significant anti-tumor capability. As immunotherapy is poised to take center stage among cancer therapies, the role of cancer vaccines remains somewhat undefined in prostate cancer, though emerging data suggest that vaccines could play a crucial therapeutic role.

titre: Prediction of biochemical recurrence after radical prostatectomy with PI-RADS version 2 in prostate cancers: initial results.
resume_court: To determine whether the Prostate Imaging Reporting and Data System version 2 (PI-RADSv2) helps predict biochemical recurrence (BCR) after radical prostatectomy for prostate cancer (PCa). No subject with a PI-RADS score <4 had BCR. Two-year, BCR-free survival post-RP was significantly lower for PI-RADS =4 (84.7-85.5 %) than for PI-RADS <4 (100 %; p?<?0.05).

titre: In Vivo Evaluation of a Bombesin Analogue Labeled with Ga-68 and Co-55/57.
resume_court: The purpose of this study was to apply an analogue of bombesin, NOTA-AMBA, labeled with Co-55 or Ga-68, for preclinical imaging of prostate cancer. NOTA-AMBA was labeled in high yields and RCP with Ga-68 and Co-55/57. Hence, for imaging, [(55)Co]NOTA-AMBA was found to be superior compared to [(68)Ga]NOTA-AMBA.

titre: Midterm functional results of taTME with neuromapping for low rectal cancer.
resume_court: Information on functional outcomes after laparoscopic-assisted transanal total mesorectal excision (taTME) is limited. Preoperative function was compared to the functional outcome 3 and 6 months, and 9 months if eligible, after stoma closure or surgery in the absence of a diverting stoma. The median LARS score was 28 (range 9-38) at 3 months and 26 (range 9-32) at 6 months (p = 0.165).

titre: Comparison of dose and catheter optimization algorithms in prostate high-dose-rate brachytherapy.
resume_court: The purpose of this work was to compare the hybrid inverse treatment planning optimization (HIPO), inverse dose-volume histogram-based optimization (DVHO), and fast simulated annealing stochastic algorithm (IPSA). For fixed catheter configurations, DVHO plans were compared with IPSA and HIPO. For dose optimization, IPSA and HIPO were not different from each other.

titre: Diagnostic and prognostic value of tissue and circulating levels of Ephrin-A2 in prostate cancer.
resume_court: Ephrin-A2, a member of the Eph/ephrin family, is associated with tumorigenesis and tumor progression. Ephrin-A2 expression was correlated with Ki-67 expression in PCa patients, both at the gene scale and protein level. Our data indicate that Ephrin-A2 is a potential diagnostic and prognostic biomarker and a promising molecular therapeutic target to attenuate prostate cancer progression.

titre: Are strict vegetarians protected against prostate cancer?
resume_court: According to the American Cancer Society, prostate cancer accounts for ~27% of all incident cancer cases among men and is the second most common (noncutaneous) cancer among men. Vegan diets showed a statistically significant protective association with prostate cancer risk (HR: 0.65; 95% CI: 0.49, 0.85). Vegan diets may confer a lower risk of prostate cancer.

titre: Extent of disease in recurrent prostate cancer determined by [(68)Ga]PSMA-HBED-CC PET/CT in relation to PSA levels, PSA doubling time and Gleason score.
resume_court: To examine the relationship between the extent of disease determined by [(68)Ga]PSMA-HBED-CC-PET/CT and the important clinical measures prostate-specific antigen (PSA), PSA doubling time (PSAdt) and Gleason score. Higher PSA levels and shorter PSAdt are independently associated with scan positivity and extrapelvic metastases, and can be used for patient selection for [(68)Ga]PSMA-HBED-CC PET/CT.

titre: Biphasic (68)Ga-PSMA-HBED-CC-PET/CT in patients with recurrent and high-risk prostate carcinoma.
resume_court: Binding of (68)Ga-PSMA-HBED-CC ((68)Ga-PSMA) at prostate cancer (PC) cells increases over time. In contrast to benign tissues, the uptake of proven tumor lesions increases on (68)Ga-PSMA-PET/CT over time. A biphasic PET-study may lead to a better detection of tumor lesions in unequivocal findings.

titre: Prognostic value of ZFP36 and SOCS3 expressions in human prostate cancer.
resume_court: ZFP36 ring finger protein (ZFP36) and the suppressor of cytokine signaling 3 (SOCS3) have been reported to, respectively, regulate NF-?B and STAT3 signaling pathways. In the present study, paired patient tissue microarrays were analyzed by immunohistochemistry, and the ZFP36 protein expression was quantitated as immunoreactive scores in patients with PCa.

titre: Genomic Correlates to the Newly Proposed Grading Prognostic Groups for Prostate Cancer.
resume_court: Recommendations by the International Society of Urologic Pathology and 2016 World Health Organization blue book propose the use of a five-tiered prostate cancer (PCa) grading system. In this study, a comprehensive analysis of the largest genomic data set on prostate cancer to date, we demonstrate molecular support for this new five-tiered system.

titre: Radiation Dose to the Penile Structures and Patient-Reported Sexual Dysfunction in Long-Term Prostate Cancer Survivors.
resume_court: The involvement of various penile structures in radiotherapy (RT)-induced sexual dysfunction among prostate cancer survivors remains unclear and domains beyond erectile dysfunction such as orgasm, and pain have typically not been considered. Sexual dysfunction following RT was separated into three main domains with symptoms related to erectile dysfunction, orgasmic dysfunction, and pain.

titre: Physical activity communication between oncology providers and patients with early-stage breast, colon, or prostate cancer.
resume_court: National guidelines recommend that patients with a cancer diagnosis engage in regular physical activity to reduce cancer-related fatigue, maintain quality of life and physical function, and improve overall prognosis and survival. In a 1-month period, 55 oncology providers had 361 encounters (clinic visits) with early-stage cancer patients. Cancer 2016;122:470-476. © 2015 American Cancer Society.

titre: VEGF-activated miR-144 regulates autophagic survival of prostate cancer cells against Cisplatin.
resume_court: Cisplatin is a commonly used chemotherapy drug for prostate cancer (PC). Together, these data suggest that cisplatin may induce VEGF to suppress miR-144 levels in PC cells, which subsequently upregulates Beclin-1 to increase autophagic cell survival against cisplatin-induced cell death. Upregulation of miR-144 or suppression of cell autophagy may improve the outcome of cisplatin therapy in PC.

titre: Tumor-associated Endo180 requires stromal-derived LOX to promote metastatic prostate cancer cell migration on human ECM surfaces.
resume_court: The diverse composition and structure of extracellular matrix (ECM) interfaces encountered by tumor cells at secondary tissue sites can influence metastatic progression. Human osteoblast-derived and fibroblast-derived ECM supported a rounded 'amoeboid-like' mode of cell migration and enhanced Endo180 expression in three prostate cancer cell lines (PC3, VCaP, DU145).

titre: Which patients benefit from post-implant CT dosimetry after real-time intraoperative planning for low dose rate prostate brachytherapy? Case series and systematic literature review.
resume_court: At present, post-implant CT-based dosimetry is a standard quality assurance practice following low dose rate (LDR) prostate brachytherapy. The real-time dosimetry parameters of 34 consecutive patients who underwent LDR brachytherapy were compared with day 30 post-implant CT-based dosimetry. Post-implant CT and dosimetry did not alter patients' management after real-time intraoperative planning.

titre: Long-term oncologic outcomes of postoperative adjuvant versus salvage radiotherapy in prostate cancer: Systemic review and meta-analysis of 5-year and 10-year follow-up data.
resume_court: There was no significant difference for the 5-year and 10-year overall survival rates between ART and SRT (RR, 0.80 and 0.94; 95% CI, 0.59-1.07 and 0.80-1.11). ART showed favorable results in BCR-free survival during the 5-year follow-up period. However, the 10-year progression-free survival and overall survival did not show any difference between ART and SRT.

titre: CyberKnife-based prostate cancer patient radioablation - early results of irradiation in 200 patients.
resume_court: Prostrate cancer (PC) is one of the most common malignancies and is frequently treated with an 8-week course of radiotherapy. The maximum percentage of late G2 toxicity was 0.7% for GI and 3.4% for GU. We conclude that CK-based radioablation in low and intermediate risk PC patients is an effective treatment modality enabling OTT reduction and presents a very low percentage of adverse effects.

titre: Optimizing the formation of vesicourethral anastomosis and reduction of procedure time. A two-year experience with a modified technique for endoscopic running vesicourethral anastomosis.
resume_court: Creation of a watertight vesicourethral anastomosis is a challenging and time-consuming procedure. Here we report our two-year experience with the Chlosta's single running suture technique. Obtained results confirm our initial observation from the preliminary report and support the use of our single running suture for the vesicourethral anastomosis in LRP.

titre: Biochemical recurrence risk factors in surgically treated high and very high-risk prostate tumors.
resume_court: High and very high-risk prostate cancers are tumors that display great variation in their progression, making their behaviour and consequent prognosis difficult to predict. The factor with the greatest influence on biochemical recurrence when it comes to surgery and high and very high-risk prostate cancer is the presence of a positive margin, followed by the Gleason score.

titre: Prostate cancer educational intervention among men in western Jamaica.
resume_court: To conduct and evaluate the impact of a theory-based health education intervention on awareness of prostate cancer and intention to screen among men in Western Jamaica and determine screening rates of men participating in the intervention at 6 months post-intervention. Statistically significant improvements in the percentage of correct responses between the pretest and posttest were evident.

titre: Analysis of miRNA expression profiling in mouse spleen affected by acute Toxoplasma gondii infection.
resume_court: Toxoplasma gondii is a worldwide prevalent pathogen that infects most of the warm-blood vertebrates. These findings will be helpful for better understanding of miRNA regulation network in host-T. gondii interaction, revealing the relationship among T. gondii infection, gene regulation, apoptosis and cancer process alterations in infected spleen.

titre: New Rates of Interventions to Manage Complications of Modern Prostate Cancer Treatment in Older Men.
resume_court: Interventions to treat complications from prostate cancer (PCa) treatment are common and affect the course of a patient's life. We examined complications after prostate cancer treatment in a large American population. Patients treated with radiotherapy rather than surgery had higher rates of complications requiring urologic procedures and rectal-anal procedures but lower rates of open surgeries.

titre: Dose impact of rectal gas on prostatic IMRT and VMAT.
resume_court: In this study, we compared the dose impact of the heterogeneity caused by rectal gas using two methods of treatment planning for intensity-modulated radiotherapy (IMRT) and volumetric-modulated arc therapy (VMAT). Values were then recalculated. However, in treatment plans for evaluation, IMRT was shown to have a higher concordance rate with standard treatment plans than VMAT.

titre: Effect of a 2-year home-based endurance training intervention on physiological function and PSA doubling time in prostate cancer patients.
resume_court: Physical activity after prostate cancer diagnosis has been shown to reduce the risk of disease progression. The control group showed no changes in any of the evaluated parameters across the 2-year intervention. In this small randomized controlled trial, we found that improvements in fitness levels correlated with increasing PSADT, suggesting a link between training and disease progression.

titre: Prostate cancer risk among users of digoxin and other antiarrhythmic drugs in the Finnish Prostate Cancer Screening Trial.
resume_court: Long-term usage of the antiarrhythmic drug digoxin has been connected to lowered risk of prostate cancer. We evaluated the association between use of digoxin, beta-blocker sotalol, and other antiarrhythmic drugs and prostate cancer risk in a retrospective cohort study. Digoxin or other antiarrhythmic drugs are not associated with any clear decrease in prostate cancer risk.

titre: Comparison of oncological and health related quality of life (HRQOL) outcomes between open (ORP) and robotic-assisted radical prostatectomy (RARP) for localized prostate cancer - findings from the population-based Victorian Prostate Cancer Registry (PCR).
resume_court: To compare the short-term oncological and HRQOL outcomes between open (ORP) and robotic-assisted (RARP) radical prostatectomy in the population-based Victorian Prostate Cancer Registry (PCR). The sexual and urinary bother at 2-year was similar between ORP and RARP. No statistically significant differences in the HRQOL outcomes between ORP and RARP were observed in multivariate analyses.

titre: A comparison of isolated circulating tumor cells and tissue biopsies using whole-genome sequencing in prostate cancer.
resume_court: Previous studies have demonstrated focal but limited molecular similarities between circulating tumor cells (CTCs) and biopsies using isolated genetic assays. These rearrangements were shared between tumor tissues and CTCs. Using high-quality WGS on single-CTCs, we identified the shared genomic alterations between CTCs and tumor tissues.

titre: Survival Outcomes of Dose-Escalated External Beam Radiotherapy versus Combined Brachytherapy for Intermediate and High Risk Prostate Cancer Using the National Cancer Data Base.
resume_court: We evaluated survival outcomes between dose-escalated EBRT (external beam radiotherapy) vs EBRT plus brachytherapy for intermediate and high risk prostate cancer using NCDB (National Cancer Data Base). Of the 20,279 study patients with prostate cancer, including 12,617 at intermediate risk and 7,662 at high risk, 71.3% received EBRT alone and 28.7% received EBRT plus brachytherapy.

titre: Outcome According to Elective Pelvic Radiation Therapy in Patients With High-Risk Localized Prostate Cancer: A Secondary Analysis of the GETUG 12 Phase 3 Randomized Trial.
resume_court: The role of pelvic elective nodal irradiation (ENI) in the management of prostate cancer is controversial. Performance of pelvic ENI was left to the treating physician. This unplanned analysis of a randomized trial failed to demonstrate a benefit of pelvic ENI on bPFS in high-risk localized prostate cancer patients.

titre: Effect of erectile dysfunction following prostate cancer treatment.
resume_court: Prostate cancer is the most prevalent non-cutaneous cancer in men worldwide. The effect of erectile dysfunction on the patient and his partner is complex; many men experience psychosocial effects influenced by their hegemonic masculine beliefs. Some men experience difficulties in addressing their needs and require support while they attempt to reframe their beliefs about masculinity.

titre: Alterations in androgen deprivation enhanced prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA) expression in prostate cancer cells as a target for diagnostics and therapy.
resume_court: Prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA) is a promising target for diagnostics and therapy of prostate carcinoma (PCa). PSMA expression increased dependently on intensified ADT in all three basic cell lines. (68)Ga-PSMA-HBED-CC uptake almost doubled during 3 h in all cell lines (p?<?0.01).

titre: Serum Proteins Enhance Dispersion Stability and Influence the Cytotoxicity and Dosimetry of ZnO Nanoparticles in Suspension and Adherent Cancer Cell Models.
resume_court: Agglomeration and sedimentation of nanoparticles (NPs) within biological solutions is a major limitation in their use in many downstream applications. In nZnO - FBS/PBS dispersions, the FBS reduced agglomeration and sedimentation behaviors to impart long-term improvements (>24 h) to the nZnO dispersion stability.

titre: Early Catheter Removal after Robot-assisted Radical Prostatectomy: Surgical Technique and Outcomes for the Aalst Technique (ECaRemA Study).
resume_court: Robot-assisted radical prostatectomy (RARP) is a widespread option for the treatment of patients with clinically localised prostate cancer. RARP was performed using the Da Vinci Si system. After catheter removal, patients in both groups showed spontaneous voiding, whereas only 11% and 8% of the patients in group A and group B experienced urinary retention after catheter removal (p=0.7).

titre: Efficacy and safety of enzalutamide in patients 75 years or older with chemotherapy-naive metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer: results from PREVAIL.
resume_court: Prostate cancer disproportionately affects older men. Elderly men benefited from treatment with enzalutamide in terms of OS and rPFS. Enzalutamide was well tolerated in the elderly subgroup and those aged <75 years.

titre: Automatic classification of prostate cancer Gleason scores from multiparametric magnetic resonance images.
resume_court: Noninvasive, radiological image-based detection and stratification of Gleason patterns can impact clinical outcomes, treatment selection, and the determination of disease status at diagnosis without subjecting patients to surgical biopsies. Separate analysis of the cancers occurring in TZ alone was not performed owing to the limited number of samples.

titre: Lack of Impact of Robotic Assisted Laparoscopic Radical Prostatectomy on Intraoperative Levels of Prostate Cancer Circulating Tumor Cells.
resume_court: While the significance of circulating tumor cells in clinically localized cancer remains controversial, it has been reported that surgical tumor manipulation can increase circulating tumor cells, including during open prostatectomy. We tested the impact of robotic assisted laparoscopic radical prostatectomy on intraoperative circulating tumor cell levels.

titre: Linking obesogenic dysregulation to prostate cancer progression.
resume_court: The global epidemic of obesity is closely linked to the development of serious co-morbidities, including many forms of cancer. Understanding the links between obesity and prostate cancer will have major implications for the health policy for men with prostate cancer and the development of new therapeutic or preventative strategies.

titre: A phase II trial of ganetespib, a heat shock protein 90 Hsp90) inhibitor, in patients with docetaxel-pretreated metastatic castrate-resistant prostate cancer (CRPC)-a prostate cancer clinical trials consortium (PCCTC) study.
resume_court: Heat shock protein 90 (Hsp90) has been studied as a therapeutic target in many cancers. Given the promising preclinical outcome and favorable pharmacologic properties of ganetespib, we conducted a phase II trial of single-agent ganetespib in patients with metastatic, castrate-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC). Ganetespib demonstrated minimal clinical activity in men with mCRPC.

titre: The clinical and therapeutic uses of MDM2 and PSMA and their potential interaction in aggressive cancers.
resume_court: Prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA) overexpression is observed in the neovasculature of solid tumors, but not in the vasculature of normal tissues. We herein review the mechanisms underlining the outgrowth of tumors associated with PSMA and MDM2, their potential interaction and how this may be applied to anticancer therapeutics.

titre: A Single Glycan at the 99-Loop of Human Kallikrein-related Peptidase 2 Regulates Activation and Enzymatic Activity.
resume_court: Human kallikrein-related peptidase 2 (KLK2) is a key serine protease in semen liquefaction and prostate cancer together with KLK3/prostate-specific antigen. Mass spectrometry revealed that Asn-95 carries a core glycan, consisting of two GlcNAc and three hexoses. These striking effects of glycosylation pave the way to a deeper understanding of kallikrein-related peptidase biology and pathology.

titre: Prostate cancer screening in Switzerland: 20-year trends and socioeconomic disparities.
resume_court: Despite important controversy in its efficacy, prostate cancer (PCa) screening has become widespread. Given the uncertainty of the usefulness of PCa screening, men, including those with high socioeconomic status, should be clearly informed about benefits and harms of PCa screening, in particular, the adverse effect of over-diagnosis and of associated over-treatment.

titre: Neuroendocrine prostate cancer
resume_court: Neuroendocrine carcinoma of the prostate (NEPC) is a rare, androgen-independent variant of prostate cancer with increasing incidence of over the past few years. Treatment of NEPC differs fundamentally compared to adenocarcinoma of the prostate. There is only limited data available for the treatment of NEPC.

titre: Dietary tocopherols inhibit PhIP-induced prostate carcinogenesis in CYP1A-humanized mice.
resume_court: Tocopherols, the major forms of vitamin E, exist as alpha-tocopherol (a-T), ß-T, ?-T and d-T. Supplementation with a ?-T-rich mixture of tocopherols (?-TmT, 0.3% in diet) significantly inhibited the development of mPIN lesions and reduced PhIP-induced elevation of 8-oxo-deoxyguanosine, COX-2, nitrotyrosine, Ki-67 and p-AKT, and the loss of PTEN and Nrf2.

titre: APPL proteins promote TGFß-induced nuclear transport of the TGFß type I receptor intracellular domain.
resume_court: The multifunctional cytokine transforming growth factor-ß (TGFß) is produced by several types of cancers, including prostate cancer, and promote tumour progression in autocrine and paracrine manners. Our results suggest that the APPL-TßRI complex promotes prostate tumour progression, and may serve as a prognostic marker.

titre: Navigating Treatment of Metastatic Castration- Resistant Prostate Cancer: Nursing Perspectives.
resume_court: Treatment of metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC) has evolved rapidly. Despite medical advances in mCRPC, studies have identified other aspects of care in which improvement is needed. Nurses can make major contributions to addressing supportive care needs, which has been shown to improve patient care and outcomes in prostate cancer.

titre: Clinical Predictors of Fatigue in Men With Non-Metastatic Prostate Cancer Receiving External Beam Radiation Therapy.
resume_court: Fatigue is one of the most distressing symptoms experienced by people with cancer receiving radiation therapy. The Functional Assessment of Cancer Therapy-Fatigue scale was administered. Heme levels at baseline and androgen-deprivation therapy (ADT) were significantly correlated with worsening of fatigue symptoms from baseline to midpoint and endpoint.

titre: Transferrin conjugates of triazacyclononane-based bifunctional NE3TA chelates for PET imaging: Synthesis, Cu-64 radiolabeling, and in vitro and in vivo evaluation.
resume_court: Three different polyaminocarboxylate-based bifunctional NE3TA (7-[2-[carboxymethyl)amino]ethyl]-1,4,7-triazacyclononane-1,4-diacetic acid) chelating agents were synthesized for potential use in copper 64-PET imaging applications. The transferrin conjugates of the NE3TA-based bifunctional chelates were evaluated for radiolabeling with (64)Cu.

titre: Multivariate piecewise exponential survival modeling.
resume_court: In this article, we develop a piecewise Poisson regression method to analyze survival data from complex sample surveys involving cluster-correlated, differential selection probabilities, and longitudinal responses, to conveniently draw inference on absolute risks in time intervals that are prespecified by investigators.

titre: Development and evaluation of a multichannel endorectal RF coil for prostate MRI at 7T in combination with an external surface array.
resume_court: To develop and evaluate a sterilizable multichannel endorectal coil (ERC) for use in combination with an external surface array (ESA) for high-resolution anatomical and functional studies of the prostate at 7T. The receive-only version of the ERC-2L improved the SNR 4.7-fold and 1.3-fold compared to the ESA and ERC-b, respectively. Imaging 2016;43:1279-1287.

titre: Relationship of Mitochondrial Enzymes to Fatigue Intensity in Men With Prostate Cancer Receiving External Beam Radiation Therapy.
resume_court: Mitochondrial dysfunction is a plausible biological mechanism for cancer-related fatigue. The HF group comprised 12 men with clinically significant change in fatigue (HF) during EBRT. Although no significant changes were observed in MOPC enzymes from baseline to EBRT completion, there were important differences in the patterns in the levels of MOPC enzymes between HF and LF groups.

titre: Exercise improves quality of life in androgen deprivation therapy-treated prostate cancer: systematic review of randomised controlled trials.
resume_court: Men receiving androgen deprivation therapy (ADT) for prostate cancer (PCa) are likely to develop metabolic conditions such as diabetes, cardiovascular disease, abdominal obesity and osteoporosis. Further studies are required to evaluate the effect of exercise and dietary interventions on QoL, androgen deprivation symptoms and metabolic risk factors in this cohort.

titre: 68Ga-PSMA-HBED-CC PET for Differential Diagnosis of Suggestive Lung Lesions in Patients with Prostate Cancer.
resume_court: In prostate cancer (PC) patients, the differentiation between lung metastases and lesions of different origin, for example, primary lung cancer, is a common clinical question. The mean SUVmax was 4.4 ± 3.9 for PC metastases and 5.6 ± 1.6 for primary lung cancer (P = 0.408). The 2 tuberculous lesions showed an SUVmax of 7.8 and 2.5.

titre: Addition of PSMA ADC to enzalutamide therapy significantly improves survival in in vivo model of castration resistant prostate cancer.
resume_court: Despite multiple new therapies available to patients with advanced castration-resistant prostate cancer (CRPC), the overall survival benefit still remains relatively short. All treatments inhibited tumor progression but with different efficacy. These results provide a strong rationale for clinical testing of PSMA ADC in combination with ENZ and/or other androgen-directed treatment strategies.

titre: Associations between circulating carotenoids, genomic instability and the risk of high-grade prostate cancer.
resume_court: Carotenoids are a class of nutrients with antioxidant properties that have been purported to protect against cancer. We examined associations between carotenoids, genotypes, tumor instability and risk of high-grade prostate cancer (Gleason grade?=?4?+?3) using logistic and linear regression. Among men with Gleason score =?3?+?4, higher lycopene levels were associated with lower FGA (P?=?0.04).

titre: A general method for the definition of margin recipes depending on the treatment technique applied in helical tomotherapy prostate plans.
resume_court: To obtain specific margin recipes that take into account the dosimetric characteristics of the treatment plans used in a single institution. We obtained dosimetric margins and margin reductions due to random errors (random margins) by fitting the theoretical results of coverages for Gaussian distributions with coverages of the planned D99% obtained from the DPHs.

titre: Structured and Modular Training Pathway for Robot-assisted Radical Prostatectomy (RARP): Validation of the RARP Assessment Score and Learning Curve Assessment.
resume_court: Use of robot-assisted radical prostatectomy (RARP) for prostate cancer is increasing. Trainees were assessed with the RARP Assessment Score by their expert mentors, and LCs for individual steps were plotted. The RARP Assessment Score based on HFMEA methodology identified critical steps for focused RARP training and assessed surgeons.

titre: Preoperative predictive factors and further risk stratification of biochemical recurrence in clinically localized high-risk prostate cancer.
resume_court: To identify preoperative predictive factors for biochemical recurrence (BCR) and to further stratify its risk in high-risk localized prostate cancer patients receiving radical prostatectomy (RP). The PPC from the dominant side and PSAD were significant independent prognostic factors for BCR. PPC from the dominant side and PSAD are significant predictors of BCR.

titre: Searching for candidate genes in familial BRCAX mutation carriers with prostate cancer.
resume_court: A family history of prostate cancer (PC) is a well-recognized high-risk factor for the development of clinically significant PC. A total of 19 truncating variants and 17 missense variants were identified for genotyping in all prostate-affected and unaffected male participants. In all, 10 truncating or missense variants showed either complete or partial segregation with PC in the relevant families.

titre: ERG overexpression and multifocality predict prostate cancer in subsequent biopsy for patients with high-grade prostatic intraepithelial neoplasia.
resume_court: The most important clinical significance of an isolated high-grade prostatic intraepithelial neoplasia (HGPIN) diagnosis is the risk of missed prostate cancer (PCa) in subsequent biopsies. Patients with ERG expression in HGPIN were more likely to have PCa in repeat biopsy, with 9 (60%) ERG-positive and 30 (21%) of ERG-negative patients having PCa (P = 0.001).

titre: Rural-Urban Differences in Costs of End-of-Life Care for Elderly Cancer Patients in the United States.
